healthcare.why: Public health risk in an overstretched health system.

2aecb7de228e.summary: A Nature study used high-throughput in vivo CAR-T double-knockout screening to find gene pairs whose combined deletion improves CAR-T antitumour activity.

cellgene.why: Identifies new edits to make CAR-T cells more potent.

tools.why: Scalable in vivo combinatorial screening method.

bc36e1dff8a6.summary: Two Nature papers map glioblastoma with single-cell and spatial multi-omics across more than a million cells, showing cancer cells follow a spatial trajectory and that non-genetic plasticity drives the disease's heterogeneity.

pharma.why: Reference atlas for designing glioblastoma treatments.

tools.why: Showcase of multi-omic atlas methods.

b8f3f77d0287.summary: A Nature study used high-throughput CRISPR interference to map interactions between essential genes in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

pharma.why: Points to combination targets for TB drugs.

tools.why: CRISPRi genetic interaction mapping in bacteria.

858ec1befcc0.summary: A Nature study shows that codon-pair-dependent ribosomal frameshifting is a feature of cancer cells and uses it to build gene circuits that switch on selectively in cancer.

cellgene.why: A new way to make gene therapies cancer-selective.

pharma.why: Possible oncology targeting strategy.

2bafaa7def40.summary: A Nature study finds endothelial cells can adapt to loss of VEGFR2 signalling and still form new functional vessels through venousization, challenging the standard view of angiogenesis.

pharma.why: May explain resistance to anti-VEGF drugs.

39fe5f95aa67.summary: Nature researchers identify Nectin-4 as the entry receptor rubella virus uses in airway and placental cells.

pharma.why: New target for understanding congenital rubella.

biosecurity.why: Clarifies how a respiratory virus infects.

52b16a1987e9.summary: A Nature gene network analysis shows mutations in diverse autism-linked genes converge on shared transcriptomic effects and sheds light on why females appear protected.

pharma.why: Convergent pathways could be drug targets.

ca7fc428671a.summary: Nature published structRFM, an open RNA foundation model pre-trained on 21 million sequence-structure pairs for predicting RNA structure and function.

ai.why: Open foundation model for RNA.

cellgene.why: Useful for designing RNA medicines.

5566a13a3b45.summary: A Nature study traces 80 years of Chinese crop breeding to a conserved flowering-time module that enables double-season cropping, and shows precision genome editing can recreate it.

agrifood.why: Genome-editing target for higher crop productivity.

269ac42effe8.summary: A Nature study of gut microbial single-nucleotide variants in 10,781 people found 940 associations linking strain-level variation to 69 health traits and exposures.

pharma.why: Leads for microbiome therapeutics.

9c3ca22fa6cf.summary: Nature reports that seizures nearly vanished in three people with epilepsy who received an experimental gene therapy, delivered by viruses into the brain and combined with a drug.

cellgene.why: Early human evidence for gene therapy in epilepsy.

pharma.why: Potential new approach for drug-resistant epilepsy.

30630a58d2fa.summary: Scientists found a compound that turns the muscle-repair protein HGF into a 'Super HGF' that binds its receptor more than twice as strongly, which could help ageing muscles repair.

pharma.why: Early-stage approach to muscle regeneration.

06c34b210643.summary: Stanford researchers used AI to identify a natural molecule that suppressed appetite and promoted fat loss in animals, which they describe as an Ozempic-like effect.

pharma.why: A new natural peptide lead in obesity.

ai.why: AI-driven discovery of a bioactive molecule.

f2f1042fa6ca.summary: Science News reports Anthropic used its Claude AI to find evidence that bacteria and viruses also likely make vaults, mysterious cell particles, suggesting an ancient origin.

ai.why: An AI model used for biological discovery.

tools.why: AI-assisted protein homology research.

d15c3500c940.summary: Senator Bernie Sanders, a pharma critic, is set to hold major sway over the FDA funding bill and could use it to push reforms, STAT reports.

pharma.why: FDA funding and drug policy could shift under a Democratic Congress.

healthcare.why: Affects FDA resources and drug access policy.

4c914e1a8e77.summary: A Korean oncologist told Korea Biomedical Review that Novartis' CDK4/6 inhibitor Kisqali (ribociclib) improved overall survival in HR+/HER2- early breast cancer much sooner than expected.

pharma.why: Overall survival backing strengthens Kisqali's adjuvant position against Verzenio.

healthcare.why: Bears on adjuvant treatment choices in early breast cancer.

647040bb5686.summary: SK bioscience's third-quarter revenue rose 21% to 182.4 billion won ($128 million), driven by its German subsidiary IDT Biologika and higher vaccine sales, while its operating loss narrowed to an 11-quarter low.

pharma.why: A major Asian vaccine maker's recovery.

bioprocessing.why: Contract manufacturing at IDT Biologika is driving growth.

bacd347a6d0e.summary: Lunit will present two studies at SITC 2026 showing its AI pathology tools can identify tissue features linked to homologous recombination deficiency in ovarian cancer and immune patterns tied to immunotherapy response in bladder cancer.

ai.why: AI pathology used to infer biomarkers from standard slides.

diagnostics.why: Could reduce reliance on separate molecular HRD tests.

b012631c9ac4.summary: Edgewise says that after an end-of-phase 2 meeting with the FDA it has submitted the protocol for STRATUS-HCM, a phase 3 program of two placebo-controlled studies of EDG-7500 in obstructive and nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, with dose escalation guided by tolerability rather than safety echocardiograms.

pharma.why: Dropping echo monitoring would differentiate EDG-7500 from approved cardiac myosin inhibitors.

investment.why: Clears the path to pivotal trials after Edgewise's recent muscular dystrophy setback.

ce19a6a8d3e4.summary: Nova Anchora raised $23 million to advance NvA-021, a topical collagen VII therapy for dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa.

pharma.why: A new entrant in a rare skin disease where Vyjuvek is approved.

investment.why: Early-stage rare disease financing.

bbe1fa005628.summary: Arcutis began enrolling a phase 3 study of Zoryve (roflumilast) cream 0.3% in moderate to severe atopic dermatitis.

pharma.why: Pushes a topical PDE4 inhibitor into more severe eczema, a market led by biologics.

9a2b317b6a51.summary: STAT reports that Sen. Bernie Sanders is likely to chair the Senate health committee next year after the midterm results, which could let him reshape how the FDA deals with drug companies.

pharma.why: A Sanders-led HELP committee would bring tougher scrutiny of drug pricing and FDA-industry ties.

healthcare.why: Raises the profile of single-payer proposals.

226e7f358d72.summary: Vericel reported third-quarter revenue up 26% to $85.4 million and net income of $14.2 million, and raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $344-346 million.

cellgene.why: A profitable commercial cell therapy company (MACI, Epicel).

investment.why: Raised guidance for a commercial-stage cell therapy business.

9dc68ad4ae72.summary: STAT reports that Rasonque, Revolution Medicines' new pancreatic cancer drug, is off to one of the best oncology drug launches in history (details behind the STAT+ paywall).

pharma.why: A first RAS(ON) inhibitor launch in pancreatic cancer selling fast signals big demand for the class.

investment.why: A strong launch reshapes Revolution Medicines' valuation and the RAS-inhibitor race.

1ac268133e22.summary: Dyne says the FDA is reviewing its BLA for z-rostudirsen in exon 51 Duchenne muscular dystrophy under priority review, with a PDUFA date of 21 January 2027.

pharma.why: A potential next-generation exon-skipping option for Duchenne.

investment.why: Sets a near-term binary decision for Dyne.

1fa222385523.summary: The UK MHRA issued interim risk-mitigation advice for Italfarmaco's Duchenne drug Duvyzat (givinostat) after several international reports of deaths in patients taking it, and has proposed updates to the product information.

pharma.why: A safety signal on one of the few approved Duchenne therapies, with likely label changes.

healthcare.why: Prescribers of Duchenne patients need to apply the new monitoring advice.

cf0c72cdf988.summary: A survey reported by Green Queen found that 60% of Indian meat-eaters like the taste of plant-based meat and eggs, but a taste gap with animal products remains and more R&D is needed.

agrifood.why: Consumer evidence for alternative protein demand in India.

d30d3f8eada9.summary: Kayak Therapeutics says the FDA cleared its IND for KT-300, a potential first-in-class TRIM7 inhibitor for RAS-driven cancers.

pharma.why: A new mechanism against RAS-driven tumours entering the clinic.

26a3f62ddbf1.summary: Opus Genetics completed dosing of the second cohort in its phase 1/2 trial of OPGx-BEST1 gene therapy for inherited retinal diseases caused by BEST1 mutations.

cellgene.why: An AAV gene therapy for an inherited retinal disease progressing through dose cohorts.

67e8de2fdade.summary: STAT looks at why shares of ProMIS Neurosciences, which is developing an Alzheimer's disease treatment, sold off sharply last week and whether the reasons hold up.

investment.why: Analysis of a sharp market reaction to an Alzheimer's biotech.

pharma.why: Bears on the outlook for a misfolded-amyloid antibody approach.

b85be3856dde.summary: Celltrion launched three biosimilars in Brazil, ustekinumab (Qoyvolma) and two denosumab products (Stoboclo, Osenvelt), taking its Brazilian portfolio to 10.

pharma.why: Shows Korean biosimilar makers expanding into Latin America.

d22c0c4a7443.summary: Curocell's CAR-T therapy Rimqarto (anbalcabtagene autoleucel) showed a 53.5% three-year overall survival rate in relapsed or refractory diffuse large B-cell lymphoma in long-term follow-up released ahead of ASH 2026.

cellgene.why: Long-term survival data for Korea's first domestic CAR-T.

pharma.why: Supports Curocell's push into second-line lymphoma.

6625d83bb3a4.summary: GI Innovation dosed the first patient in a global phase 1b/2 trial combining its GI-102 with Johnson & Johnson's KLK2xCD3 T-cell engager pasritamig in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer.

pharma.why: A Korean biotech in a clinical collaboration with J&J.

3d7a610b67ec.summary: The UK MHRA and NICE published a report on a joint scientific dialogue on real-world evidence, aimed at supporting both regulatory and health technology assessment decisions across a product's lifecycle.

pharma.why: Aligns UK regulator and HTA body on how real-world evidence will be judged.

healthcare.why: Could speed NHS access decisions.

1e42da2fb1a0.summary: UKHSA published the latest Gonococcal Resistance to Antimicrobials Surveillance Programme (GRASP) report on trends in resistance and reduced susceptibility in gonorrhoea in England and Wales.

biosecurity.why: Tracks drug-resistant gonorrhoea, a WHO priority pathogen.

healthcare.why: Informs treatment guidance for sexually transmitted infections.

3c0c6cc9b7e9.summary: STAT reports that after patient deaths China has restricted investigator-initiated biotech trials, slowing a flood of fast early human studies and leaving rare-disease families and US investors facing uncertainty.

pharma.why: Investigator-initiated trials in China have been a fast, cheap route to early human data for global drug developers.

investment.why: Weakens a key source of quick proof-of-concept data behind China in-licensing deals.

cellgene.why: Many such trials tested cell and gene therapies.

8d0c293fe017.summary: Cloudbreak Pharma's CBT-001 eye drops beat vehicle in a 659-patient phase 3 trial in pterygium, improving eye redness at month 3 and slowing lesion growth at month 12 (both p<0.001); superficial keratitis was more common on drug (20% vs 8%). Cloudbreak, whose Hong Kong shares have been suspended since September, plans to meet the FDA.

pharma.why: Potentially the first drug for pterygium, a condition now treated only by surgery.

investment.why: Results come as the company's listed shares remain suspended.

eeece3668fba.summary: Oxford spinout Alethio Therapeutics raised a $90 million Series A, about a year after leaving stealth, to advance its lead antibody for essential thrombocythemia and other myeloproliferative neoplasms.

pharma.why: A new antibody approach in rare blood cancers now treated mostly with JAK inhibitors and cytoreduction.

investment.why: A large Series A for a UK university spinout.

2f07e95d5e1c.summary: A day after Texas elected Democratic statewide leaders, two cultivated meat companies urged a court to overturn the state's ban on cultivated meat, Green Queen reports.

agrifood.why: Texas is one of the US states banning cultivated meat sales.

fermentation.why: State bans shape the US market for cell-cultured food.

87bdd90929ca.summary: Implantica says the first US procedures with its RefluxStop implant for acid reflux have been completed.

meddevices.why: US commercial entry for a new reflux implant.

8c1ec69c7408.summary: Acepodia dosed the first patient in a phase 1 trial of ACE723, a dual-payload antibody-drug conjugate and the first candidate from its AD2C platform.

pharma.why: Dual-payload ADCs are an emerging design to overcome resistance.

a90da742718e.summary: Compass Pathways published survey data on the burden of treatment-resistant depression on patients and caregivers as it prepares to launch its psilocybin therapy COMP360, which is nearing the market.

pharma.why: Groundwork for what could be the first approved psychedelic medicine.

healthcare.why: Psychedelic therapy needs new clinic infrastructure and payer buy-in.

e8d1151d856f.summary: Novonesis reported 7% organic sales growth for the first nine months of 2026 and an adjusted EBITDA margin of 37.9%, confirming its full-year outlook of 7-8% growth.

industrial.why: The largest industrial enzymes and microbes company sets the tone for industrial biotech demand.

fermentation.why: Novonesis is the biggest player in precision-fermented enzymes and cultures.

agrifood.why: Food, feed and agricultural biosolutions are a large part of its sales.

5242c89f8c10.summary: Cambridge, UK biotech T-Therapeutics raised an oversubscribed $133 million Series B, with J&J, Merck KGaA and Eli Lilly joining Sanofi, to take its TCR-based T cell engagers for cancer and autoimmune disease to clinical proof of concept.

pharma.why: Four big pharma investors back TCR bispecifics, including for autoimmune disease.

investment.why: One of the larger European private rounds this year.

6088289a42ae.summary: Telix joined Thera4Care, a European initiative to build an integrated theranostics ecosystem, with its FAP-targeting candidate TLX400-Tx selected for evaluation with terbium-161.

pharma.why: Radiopharmaceutical companies are pooling efforts on next-generation isotopes.

healthcare.why: Aims to widen theranostics access in Europe.

099deddd2dc1.summary: Akeso says China's NMPA granted priority review to ivonescimab plus chemotherapy for first-line locally advanced or metastatic biliary tract cancer.

pharma.why: Extends the PD-1xVEGF bispecific, the most watched new oncology class, into a new indication.

investment.why: Adds to Akeso's and partner Summit's commercial runway in China.

88ca828ec76d.summary: A Nature Medicine study of fecal metagenomes from 6,803 adults in Japan's 4D cohort, validated in 13 other cohorts, found two opposing microbiome-mediated axes that link modifiable lifestyle factors to health and chronic disease.

healthcare.why: Microbiome scores could become markers for lifestyle-linked disease risk.

diagnostics.why: Validated microbiome prediction scores are a step towards stool-based risk tests.

tools.why: Large-scale shotgun metagenomics across many cohorts.

2c80c0c9f787.summary: A bioRxiv preprint maps a Mg-Fe-PmrAB regulatory circuit that makes Enterobacteriaceae tolerant to polymyxins under phosphate starvation, and reports that targeting it reverses that tolerance. Not yet peer-reviewed.

pharma.why: Points to a way to restore polymyxins, a last-resort antibiotic class.

biosecurity.why: Relevant to antimicrobial resistance in Gram-negative pathogens.

bba62f9188b5.summary: NEJM published an original trial report on Arrowhead's RNAi drug plozasiran in severe hypertriglyceridemia, including its effect on the risk of acute pancreatitis (full text not accessible).

pharma.why: Key evidence for expanding plozasiran beyond familial chylomicronaemia syndrome into a much larger population.

healthcare.why: Pancreatitis prevention is the clinically meaningful outcome for these patients.

4adefc7ac51d.summary: An NEJM editorial discusses the trial results for a triple incretin agonist in obesity, knee osteoarthritis and obstructive sleep apnea.

pharma.why: Commentary on the obesity drug class's expansion into new indications.

422f64f06226.summary: WuXi Biologics and Fresenius struck what Endpoints calls one of the largest biosimilar deals to date, ahead of an expected 'golden decade' of biologic patent expiries.

bioprocessing.why: Gives a Chinese CDMO a major role in a European biosimilar pipeline despite US Biosecure pressure.

pharma.why: Biosimilar players are positioning for a large wave of biologic patent losses.

81218e82cb20.summary: OliX Pharmaceuticals submitted an IND to the FDA to run part of a phase 2a trial of OLX301A, its RNAi treatment for geographic atrophy, after Australian approval of the study.

pharma.why: An siRNA approach to geographic atrophy moving into US trials.

dda88121b0a4.summary: AdvaMed chair and Resmed CEO Mick Farrell told MedTech Dive his priorities for the medtech industry in a year of cyberattacks, inflation and possible tariffs.

meddevices.why: Industry lobby priorities on tariffs and regulation.

a7d625909f35.summary: An NEJM editorial discusses the evidence on sirolimus-coated balloon angioplasty for infrainguinal (leg) artery disease.

meddevices.why: Drug-coated balloons are a growing alternative to stents in peripheral artery disease.

06e27e10adae.summary: The Scientist reports that Merck and Moderna's personalised mRNA cancer vaccine, added to standard care, cut the risk of melanoma recurrence or death by 42%.

cellgene.why: Personalised mRNA vaccine data in melanoma.

pharma.why: Supports individualised neoantigen therapy as a category.

2330167c4bc4.summary: A Labiotech piece from Lonza discusses the 'stranded asset' problem in microbial custom manufacturing, where capacity built for one product goes unused.

bioprocessing.why: Capacity planning in microbial CDMO manufacturing.

fermentation.why: Relevant to companies relying on contract microbial capacity.

085276735ab6.summary: A Lancet editorial marks ten years of the Lancet Countdown on health and climate change and asks what should come next.

healthcare.why: Climate effects on health systems.

4f4674650ee8.summary: Lancet editor Richard Horton argues China's late nomination of Song Li for WHO Director-General reflects its bid to lead global health.

healthcare.why: Future WHO leadership.

biosecurity.why: WHO direction shapes outbreak response.

6a80f0602045.summary: The Global Fund appointed Mark Dybul, a former US global AIDS coordinator, as its head.

healthcare.why: Leadership of a major global health funder.

6d372a0bc57e.summary: After a Supreme Court ruling, India's National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority will cap trade margins on 137 cancer drugs, The Lancet reports.

pharma.why: Price controls in a large market for cancer drugs.

healthcare.why: Aims to make cancer treatment cheaper in India.

feb3abe5b5e0.summary: The Tumaini trial has begun testing vaccines against Bundibugyo virus, the Ebola strain behind an outbreak that has killed more than 5,000 people in DR Congo, The Lancet reports.

biosecurity.why: First vaccine trial for the Ebola strain in a large ongoing outbreak.

pharma.why: Vaccine development for an outbreak pathogen.

healthcare.why: Outbreak response in Central Africa.

732005ca2f6b.summary: FX Shoulder Solutions says the FDA cleared Easytech Reversed, which it calls the first stemless reverse shoulder replacement system in the US.

meddevices.why: First-in-class orthopaedic implant clearance.

d387acb16c52.summary: Brii Bio says phase 2 ENRICH and ENHANCE data at AASLD support using its vaccine BRII-179 to prime immune responses and raise hepatitis B functional cure rates with siRNA drugs.

pharma.why: Combination strategy for HBV functional cure.

1e30bc7bb1bd.summary: AusperBio says hepatitis B functional cure with its antisense drug AHB-137 was maintained in 16 of 17 evaluable previously treated patients at 12 months off all therapy, in late-breaking AASLD data.

pharma.why: Durability data in the race for an HBV functional cure.

healthcare.why: Finite therapy for chronic hepatitis B.

03fead43962c.summary: The FDA granted accelerated approval to J&J's subcutaneous Rybrevant Faspro (amivantamab and hyaluronidase) for recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma that progressed on or after platinum chemotherapy.

pharma.why: New indication for a J&J bispecific in a hard-to-treat cancer.

healthcare.why: New option for relapsed head and neck cancer.

27cffe388e6c.summary: PhRMA spent an estimated $59 million on search advertising over seven years to shape how Americans view drug prices, STAT reports.

pharma.why: Industry lobbying on drug pricing.

fa98297baefc.summary: Novartis confirmed nine reported cases of tumours in children treated with its spinal muscular atrophy gene therapy Zolgensma, seven disclosed for the first time; two may be linked to integration of the viral vector's DNA. More than 6,000 patients have been treated since its 2019 approval.

cellgene.why: Raises the question of AAV vector integration and cancer risk across gene therapy.

pharma.why: Safety signal for a marketed Novartis product.

healthcare.why: Affects long-term monitoring of treated children.

bcda996e5bd5.summary: Medicare finalized a rule that will cut billions in payments for drugs bought through the 340B discount programme and expand site-neutral payments between care settings from 2027. Hospitals strongly oppose it.

healthcare.why: Cuts hospital revenue from 340B drugs and outpatient sites.

pharma.why: Reshapes the 340B discount system drugmakers have fought over for years.

investment.why: Shifts margins between hospitals and drugmakers.

dfcc432e7698.summary: Cryoport's Q3 revenue rose 14% to $50.2 million, with commercial cell and gene therapy revenue up 20%; it supports 788 clinical trials and 23 approved cell and gene therapies.

bioprocessing.why: Supply-chain demand indicator for advanced therapies.

cellgene.why: Tracks commercial cell and gene therapy activity.

4df58a8cb497.summary: Endpoints feature on preeclampsia, a dangerous pregnancy complication with no approved drugs, and the first medicines now in development for it.

pharma.why: A neglected indication drawing new drug development.

healthcare.why: Major cause of maternal and infant harm.

e6d4e184a41d.summary: An infant in southwestern Wisconsin died after contracting measles, the state's first measles death since 1990.

healthcare.why: Another US measles death as cases rise.

biosecurity.why: Resurgence of a vaccine-preventable disease.

c8e95611a059.summary: Researchers used AI-guided protein engineering to design a broadly protective H5Nx bird flu vaccine that outperformed current stockpiled vaccines in preclinical tests.

biosecurity.why: Pandemic preparedness against current and future H5 strains.

ai.why: AI-designed vaccine antigen.

pharma.why: Next-generation influenza vaccine design.

94d62f95bcef.summary: The CEO of the American Academy of Family Physicians plans to ask Congress for legal guardrails to protect the CDC's vaccine advisory committee ACIP after more than a year of turmoil.

healthcare.why: US vaccine recommendations guide clinical practice and coverage.

pharma.why: ACIP decisions drive vaccine sales.

c30fa5cbf5bf.summary: VintaBio, a viral-vector CDMO launched in 2023 for cell and gene therapy, is putting its manufacturing facility and IP up for sale as vector demand slows.

bioprocessing.why: Sign of overcapacity in viral-vector manufacturing.

cellgene.why: Reflects the slowdown in cell and gene therapy.

ff1b49ebba4d.summary: Alnylam's chief commercial officer of six years, Tolga Tanguler, is leaving as sales of Amvuttra fall short of expectations.

pharma.why: Leadership change at a major RNAi company amid a sales slowdown.

00413350b90d.summary: The FDA accused Vanda of creating a misleading impression of the safety and effectiveness of its motion-sickness drug Nereus in a TV ad.

pharma.why: FDA enforcement on drug advertising.

3e39974a9c9d.summary: ANI Pharmaceuticals agreed to buy Swedish drugmaker Egetis Therapeutics for $560 million, gaining Emcitate, the only approved treatment for MCT8 deficiency.

pharma.why: Rare disease M&A for an approved orphan drug.

investment.why: Takeout of a listed European biotech.

145d7ea180e7.summary: Evommune paid China's Hinova Pharmaceuticals $30 million upfront in a deal worth up to about $1 billion for a preclinical molecular glue degrader, a niche Novartis is also pursuing.

pharma.why: Another China-sourced asset for a US biotech.

investment.why: Deal size and upfront benchmark for China licensing.

85101ab8f79e.summary: AstraZeneca has offered roughly $10 billion for rare obesity drugmaker Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, the Wall Street Journal reports; analysts expect a possible bidding war and doubt Rhythm will accept the current offer.

pharma.why: Large potential obesity acquisition by AstraZeneca.

investment.why: Possible bidding war for a mid-cap biotech.

fdc732fce536.summary: Agios plans to cut more than 100 R&D roles by the end of 2026 as it prepares for a hoped-for sickle cell approval of mitapivat.

pharma.why: R&D cuts at a commercial-stage rare disease company.

f12e1db0df6c.summary: German biotech Vivoryon regained China rights to its kidney disease candidate from Simcere as its cash runs low.

pharma.why: Partnership unwinding at a cash-strapped biotech.

a2d74786959d.summary: MetaVia says its GLP-1/glucagon agonist reduced liver fat and body weight in a phase 1 trial and plans a phase 2 in alcohol-associated liver disease next year.

pharma.why: Early incretin data in liver disease.

e9a0539daa4c.summary: Rezera, the renamed NodThera, is seeking a $181 million IPO to take its NLRP3 inhibitor into phase 3 for a cardiovascular disease.

investment.why: Another sizeable biotech IPO in a reopening window.

pharma.why: Funds a phase 3 test of NLRP3 inhibition in heart disease.

610712a85cde.summary: A panel of US medical societies endorsed influenza, RSV and COVID-19 vaccine recommendations for respiratory clinicians, offering a single reference during the transition in national immunisation advice.

healthcare.why: Professional societies filling the gap left by changes at ACIP.

pharma.why: Affects vaccine uptake.

55f8478c605b.summary: The nonprofit Orphan Therapeutics Accelerator in-licensed its first gene therapy and plans to expand its pipeline.

cellgene.why: Nonprofit model for rare-disease gene therapies.

6cb8c97e0e47.summary: Varda Space Industries says its W-8 capsule returned safely from orbit while two other vehicles remain in space, its first multi-vehicle operation for orbital pharmaceutical processing.

bioprocessing.why: Progress in in-space drug crystallisation and processing.

pharma.why: Potential new route for drug formulation.

5f8931a76a44.summary: J&J, AbbVie and others will show early data at ASH for trispecific antibodies in multiple myeloma, drugs that hit three targets at once and could follow bispecifics as the next step in treatment.

pharma.why: Next wave of myeloma antibodies from large drugmakers.

cellgene.why: Trispecifics compete with CAR-T in myeloma.

cf7568fc10ae.summary: Edwards Lifesciences raised its sales forecast after strong TAVR sales in Q3 and expects procedure volumes to rise on positive trial data and expanded Medicare reimbursement.

meddevices.why: Demand outlook for transcatheter heart valves.

d0b56cf11a74.summary: Genmab published its results for the first nine months of 2026.

pharma.why: Results from a major antibody company.

3317678000ad.summary: The UK MHRA published a 2026–2030 plan to broaden patient and public involvement in medicines and device regulation and show how patient experience informs its decisions.

healthcare.why: Changes how UK regulation uses patient input.

pharma.why: UK regulator process change.

meddevices.why: Covers device regulation too.

7438ebf450ee.summary: UKHSA issued guidance on using combined COVID-19 and influenza A+B rapid antigen tests during respiratory infection outbreaks in adult care homes.

diagnostics.why: Official use case for combo rapid tests.

healthcare.why: Outbreak management in care homes.

866c63244f9b.summary: Two more US biotechs licensed autoimmune drugs from China: Caldera Therapeutics took an IL-17xTL1A bispecific antibody from partner Qyuns, and Evommune an oral VAV1 molecular glue degrader from Hinova.

pharma.why: Continues the steady flow of China in-licensing deals.

investment.why: Shows how US startups source assets.

b6ba4e7aef7d.summary: Merck's GLP-1/glucagon agonist efinopegdutide, licensed from Hanmi, cleared a phase 2b MASH trial at AASLD, with MASH resolution in 63% of patients on the 7 mg dose versus 13% on placebo.

pharma.why: Strong biopsy data in the crowded MASH and incretin race.

healthcare.why: MASH is a large unmet liver disease.

2051e46c166c.summary: Resolution Therapeutics says 2 of 9 patients with end-stage liver disease given its macrophage cell therapy RTX001 died, needed a transplant or decompensated within six months, versus 8 of 21 in an external control group (interim, non-randomised data, to be presented at AASLD).

cellgene.why: Early data for a regenerative macrophage cell therapy.

pharma.why: New approach to end-stage liver disease.

c62ac319b0da.summary: Ellipsis Health, which uses voice AI to screen and call patients, acquired Kouper Health, Endpoints reports.

ai.why: Consolidation in healthcare voice-AI startups.

healthcare.why: AI calling for patient follow-up.

847b4a606960.summary: In a real-world study of more than 500,000 statin users with high LDL cholesterol, Amgen's Repatha was linked to a 20% lower heart attack risk than ezetimibe (Zetia), STAT reports.

pharma.why: Comparative evidence for PCSK9 inhibitors versus cheap generics.

healthcare.why: Guides add-on cholesterol treatment choices.

6b74d6ad5554.summary: A Science paper presents nanoswitch screening, a method for discovering molecules that modulate biomolecular targets.

tools.why: New screening platform for drug discovery.

pharma.why: Hit-finding method.

b4712731a57d.summary: A Science study finds that tumour metastasis co-opts blood-cell production in the liver to promote immunosuppression.

pharma.why: New mechanism of immune evasion in metastatic cancer.

5b32d3aa2877.summary: A Science review examines the evidence on obesity drugs and cognition.

pharma.why: Potential brain effects of GLP-1 class drugs.

healthcare.why: Relevant to long-term use of obesity drugs.

8a02c7f3e31c.summary: A Science perspective weighs the evidence on GLP-1 therapies and cancer risk.

pharma.why: Safety question for the biggest drug class.

healthcare.why: Relevant to long-term GLP-1 use.

ac4413a3e10a.summary: An international team has published the first coordinated guidelines for phage therapy against antibiotic-resistant infections, ScienceDaily reports.

pharma.why: Standards for an emerging antimicrobial approach.

healthcare.why: Option against resistant infections.

bf0901e0f445.summary: Researchers describe a Staphylococcus phage recombination cassette that enables recombineering (precise genome editing with phage recombinases) across distantly related bacteria, rather than needing a new system for each species. Not yet peer-reviewed.

tools.why: A broad-host genome-editing tool for bacteria.

industrial.why: Could ease engineering of non-model production microbes.

53e9299fcc14.summary: In mice engineered to carry the human transferrin receptor, the number of receptor-binding sites on an Fc-FGF21 fusion set its half-life and its weight-loss effect. Not yet peer-reviewed.

pharma.why: Design lesson for long-acting FGF21 obesity drugs.

96fe1e338a8d.summary: A preprint describes a droplet single-cell RNA sequencing method that profiles cells while they are still alive, instead of requiring them to be fixed or lysed first. Not yet peer-reviewed.

tools.why: New single-cell sequencing workflow.

46c8905d2153.summary: COSMOS is a metagenomics approach that monitors mosquito vectors and the pathogens they carry from the same samples, aimed at surveillance of mosquito-borne disease. Not yet peer-reviewed.

biosecurity.why: Combined vector and pathogen surveillance for outbreak warning.

tools.why: Sequencing-based surveillance method.

004dfe9fab63.summary: An individual-patient meta-analysis of randomised trials in The Lancet found low short-term adverse event rates with both 0/1 hour and 0/3 hour troponin pathways for suspected heart attack in the emergency department.

diagnostics.why: Evidence on fast troponin testing pathways.

healthcare.why: Affects emergency department throughput.

901dde8315bc.summary: The 2026 Lancet Countdown report on health and climate change finds a decade of escalating health harms from climate change and calls this a decisive moment for action.

healthcare.why: Flagship tracking report on climate-driven health harms.

agrifood.why: Covers climate effects on food security.

53c4b7f68d10.summary: In the phase 3 HERON-Lung01 trial in China, the ADC ruzaltatug rezetecan significantly prolonged progression-free survival versus chemotherapy in EGFR-mutated lung cancer that had progressed on EGFR inhibitors (interim analysis, The Lancet).

pharma.why: Phase 3 win for a China-developed ADC.

healthcare.why: New option after EGFR inhibitor resistance.

36a8a788b4ca.summary: Fathom Therapeutics raised a $55 million Series A led by Sutter Hill Ventures, with Kos Biotechnology Partners joining, according to Kos. Fathom's Microcosmos platform combines quantum chemistry, physics-based simulation and AI to model protein-drug interactions at atomic resolution.

ai.why: Venture backing for physics-plus-AI drug discovery.

pharma.why: A new discovery-platform company aiming to generate drug candidates.

investment.why: A sizeable Series A for an AI discovery startup.

2a21ff38ff0b.summary: Satellos says that after FDA feedback it has changed the primary endpoint of its phase 2 BASECAMP trial of oral forazapadin in boys aged 7 to 9 with Duchenne muscular dystrophy from dynamometry to MRI-measured fat fraction of the vastus lateralis. Topline 12-week placebo-controlled data are expected in Q1 2027.

pharma.why: Shows FDA openness to an MRI imaging endpoint in a Duchenne trial.

healthcare.why: Rare paediatric muscle disease programme.

f21a1250ffa0.summary: Zimmer Biomet announced Surgeon-Guided Autonomy, which it calls a new category of intelligent surgery built on a closed-loop 'predict, perform, recover' framework that keeps the surgeon in control in the operating room.

meddevices.why: A large orthopaedics maker's strategy for autonomous features in surgical robotics.

ai.why: AI-driven planning and autonomy in surgery.

4d519828704c.summary: INOVIO priced a public offering of about $75 million, days after FDA approval of its DNA-based immunotherapy Voceryq for recurrent respiratory papillomatosis.

pharma.why: Funds the launch of a newly approved DNA medicine.

investment.why: Post-approval equity raise.

cellgene.why: DNA medicine platform.

786b1e94c068.summary: Lynk Pharmaceuticals says China's NMPA has accepted its new drug application for zemprocitinib, its lead drug, in rheumatoid arthritis.

pharma.why: A China-developed JAK-class immunology drug nears approval.

0d08b919c0c7.summary: Bio-Thera says China's NMPA approved BAT2506, the first golimumab biosimilar approved in China.

pharma.why: First biosimilar competition for golimumab in China.

bioprocessing.why: Another biologic biosimilar entering manufacture.

7e4ce0537f43.summary: Endpoints rounds up executive moves: Novo Nordisk and Pfizer have hired new chief financial officers, and Alnylam's chief commercial officer is leaving as its commercial struggles continue.

pharma.why: Leadership changes at three large drugmakers.

investment.why: CFO changes at Novo and Pfizer matter to investors.

20446dc6d8dd.summary: Merck Life Science CEO Jean-Charles Wirth told Korea Biomedical Review the company plans to grow its newly opened Daejeon bioprocessing production centre into a regional hub serving Korea and other Asian markets, possibly adding products as demand grows.

bioprocessing.why: A major bioprocess supplier is building Asian manufacturing capacity.

tools.why: Life-science supply chain in Asia.

304594adf3d0.summary: Pfizer's Litfulo (ritlecitinib) cleared Korea's HIRA reimbursement review for severe alopecia areata in adults and adolescents aged 12 and over, moving it closer to national insurance coverage.

pharma.why: Reimbursement step for a Pfizer immunology drug in Korea.

healthcare.why: Wider patient access in Korea.

09eefb74c4c2.summary: SK biopharmaceuticals says it built a 7.14-million-record dataset and tested a specialised AI model on 66 drug development tasks in a government-backed project, but has not disclosed the model's performance.

ai.why: Korean government-backed push to build drug R&D AI models.

pharma.why: AI tools for drug development at a Korean drugmaker.

cdfca44fb81f.summary: Korea's MFDS designated two peritoneal dialysis devices, including a US-made PD catheter, for emergency import to treat severe acute kidney injury in newborns and children.

meddevices.why: Emergency import route to fill a paediatric device gap.

healthcare.why: Access to dialysis for critically ill children.

8937d08a28c4.summary: A Nature paper describes an AI system that coordinates laboratory instruments to run multi-step molecular biology experiments with limited human intervention; Nature's news team reports the self-driving lab in China needs only a simple prompt to encode messages in DNA and read them out.

ai.why: AI agents running real wet-lab workflows end to end.

tools.why: Lab automation that could change how experiments are run.

3cf1b441539c.summary: A gait foundation model trained on 3D skeletal motion from 3,328 adults predicts a wide range of clinical characteristics and diagnoses, Nature Medicine reports.

ai.why: A foundation model applied to motion data for health prediction.

diagnostics.why: Gait as a non-invasive screening signal for many conditions.

meddevices.why: Points to camera or sensor-based assessment tools.

b94e0a289435.summary: Cas12a-based combinatorial knockout screens produced a genetic interaction map of the DNA damage response, defining functional relationships among its genes and pathways (Nature Biotechnology).

tools.why: Combinatorial CRISPR screening method and resource.

pharma.why: Synthetic-lethal targets in DNA repair for oncology.

b675c84de30c.summary: NYU Grossman researchers found that DNA replication problems at a small set of chromosome sites can determine how cancer cells respond to PARP inhibitors, pointing to possible biomarkers of drug sensitivity.

pharma.why: Could help select patients for PARP inhibitors.

6849fb47c61f.summary: Multi-omic analyses of patient glioblastoma cells in Nature show non-genetic cellular plasticity drives disease progression, with the stability of cell states shaping how tumours evolve.

pharma.why: Regulatory programmes as targets in an untreatable brain cancer.

tools.why: Multi-omic profiling at scale.

bd4cdf44eda9.summary: A Nature News & Views piece describes how errors in protein production from RNA in cancer cells might be harnessed for a gene-therapy tool that selectively targets tumours.

cellgene.why: A new tumour-selective gene therapy concept.

pharma.why: Oncology modality at early research stage.

03257a465565.summary: TomoSAXS, an X-ray imaging platform shown on intervertebral discs, visualises mechanics from the nanoscale to the whole organ in intact tissue (Nature).

tools.why: New multiscale imaging method for tissue mechanics.

meddevices.why: Relevant to spinal implant and tissue research.

deb9f5661d3e.summary: Global heat-related mortality rose by 29% in very strong El Niño years, with the heaviest burden in low- and middle-income countries, according to epidemiological estimates in Nature Medicine.

healthcare.why: Quantifies climate-cycle health burden for planning.

a7634ba5b2eb.summary: A preprint reports high reproducibility in one direct-to-consumer gut microbiome testing workflow under real-world conditions, using fecal reference material. Not yet peer-reviewed.

diagnostics.why: Addresses known variability in consumer microbiome tests.

tools.why: Use of reference materials for microbiome assays.

cb775cce66ff.summary: MitoDecode quantifies mitochondrial stress states directly from fluorescence images without segmentation or predefined features, a preprint reports. Not yet peer-reviewed.

tools.why: Image-analysis method for cell phenotyping.

ai.why: Learned image decoding of cell states.

b20726548707.summary: A mouse study preprint tests whether nanotherapy-induced tolerance of allogeneic islet grafts survives a distant MRSA skin infection, relevant to replacing lifelong immunosuppression in islet transplantation for type 1 diabetes. Not yet peer-reviewed.

cellgene.why: Durability of tolerance for cell transplant therapies.

pharma.why: Immune tolerance approaches in diabetes.

7c4c17589a33.summary: Slovenian food-tech startup Juicy Marbles launched Granny's Roast, a whole-cut plant-based turkey roulade, for Thanksgiving.

agrifood.why: Product launch in whole-cut plant-based meat.

416f9d687684.summary: Verigraft's CEO told BioProcess International how its tissue-engineered vein grafts aim to treat chronic vein disease without the risk of rejection.

cellgene.why: Tissue-engineered graft approach to vein disease.

bioprocessing.why: Manufacture of engineered tissue.

b3710bf97619.summary: An implantable ultrasound patch tracked spinal cord blood flow and delivered localised therapy after surgery in animal models, The Scientist reports.

meddevices.why: Implantable monitoring and therapy device for spinal cord injury.

c7627b987300.summary: George Church has quit as an adviser to AI startup Radical Numerics, alleging it erased its partner Tabula's role in its first AI-designed phage therapy.

ai.why: Credit dispute over an AI-designed therapy.

tools.why: Concerns the AI biology startup scene.

fbc130a12e1b.summary: InMed Pharmaceuticals has closed its merger with Mentari Therapeutics and taken the Mentari name; shares will trade on Nasdaq as MTRI from 9 November.

investment.why: Reverse-merger route to Nasdaq.

5b790c4dec3b.summary: Hengrui and Braveheart Bio say their cardiac myosin inhibitor HRS/BHB-1893 gave durable reductions in LVOT gradient and better exercise capacity at 52 weeks in a phase 2 extension in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, presented at AHA.

pharma.why: A China-originated rival in the myosin inhibitor class.

24952babf34a.summary: Novo says real-world studies at AASLD linked Wegovy 2.4 mg to lower liver enzymes, weight and blood sugar in MASH, including 8.6 kg mean weight loss versus resmetirom at six months.

pharma.why: Real-world comparison of semaglutide with resmetirom in MASH.

healthcare.why: Informs treatment choice in MASH.

2845a335803d.summary: Contract Pharma reports that AI drug discovery company Chai Discovery and Roche will collaborate on AI drug discovery; terms are not given in the headline.

ai.why: Adds Roche to Chai's growing list of big-pharma partners.

pharma.why: Big pharma keeps buying into AI molecule design.

a15fc72e88c1.summary: Lilly successfully challenged Good Life Meds' health-benefit and personalisation claims for a compounded tirzepatide product, forcing it to drop them.

pharma.why: Lilly's continuing campaign against compounded GLP-1 copies.

healthcare.why: Affects how compounded weight-loss drugs are marketed.

24de8f2187bd.summary: Generate Biomedicines' CEO says the Flagship company used Anthropic's Claude to shrink the size of CAR-T cell engines, and sees a huge opportunity in AI tools.

ai.why: General-purpose AI models applied to cell therapy design.

cellgene.why: Smaller CAR constructs can ease delivery and manufacturing.

94c6ae8aa158.summary: After its norovirus vaccine missed in phase 3, Moderna has scrapped plans to enrol a new cohort and will meet regulators to decide next steps.

pharma.why: Setback for the only late-stage norovirus vaccine.

biosecurity.why: Leaves no near-term vaccine for a major outbreak pathogen.

cellgene.why: Another mRNA vaccine failure outside Covid.

1ff1f621de94.summary: Merck has dropped the Sutro Biopharma-partnered IL-2 agonist it was testing in solid tumours, calling it routine pipeline prioritisation.

pharma.why: Another big-pharma exit from engineered IL-2.

cac485472c39.summary: Natera unexpectedly named Solomon Moshkevich CEO, a change that set off a stock selloff on Friday, analysts said.

diagnostics.why: Leadership change at a leading genetic testing company.

investment.why: Shares fell on the surprise.

197d636f0701.summary: At SITC, Immunocore said an estimated 70% of first-line metastatic uveal melanoma patients given its bispecific brenetafusp plus Kimmtrak were alive at two years (17 patients; median survival not reached at 29 months).

pharma.why: Early test of combining two T-cell engagers in a solid tumour.

c57c5a42df62.summary: A study found women with higher blood levels of two common PFAS chemicals were more likely to develop oestrogen receptor-negative breast cancer, GEN reports.

healthcare.why: Adds evidence on environmental cancer risk.

diagnostics.why: Possible role for PFAS exposure testing.

70594aac9321.summary: Zydus says 39.1% of MASH patients on saroglitazar 4 mg and 32.4% on 2 mg had steatohepatitis resolution without fibrosis worsening at 52 weeks in phase 2b, versus 13.7% on placebo (AASLD 2026).

pharma.why: Adds an oral PPAR agonist to the crowded MASH field.

5536e573e839.summary: Evaxion says new biomarker data from the phase 2 trial of its AI-designed personalised cancer vaccine EVX-01 in advanced melanoma show strong immune responses.

ai.why: Data from an AI-designed personalised neoantigen vaccine.

pharma.why: Early immunogenicity data only.

f034209d64ee.summary: Tandem Diabetes Care named Jeannette Bankes CEO; John Sheridan retires at year end after leading the company since 2019.

meddevices.why: New leader at a major insulin pump maker.

7eec992bb90f.summary: Siemens Healthineers will carve out its in vitro diagnostics business, rebranded as Olyrian Diagnostics, as a standalone company by mid-2028.

diagnostics.why: Creates a new standalone IVD company from one of the largest players.

meddevices.why: Reshapes Siemens Healthineers around imaging.

investment.why: Possible future listing or sale of the IVD unit.

a97afda286b5.summary: BioSpace reports that the FlowStop haemostatic spray has reached 18,000 units and its maker is seeking FDA clearance.

meddevices.why: A bleeding-control device heading for FDA review.

29f740ab275c.summary: Sarepta will stop enrolling patients in the phase 3 trial of its Duchenne gene therapy Elevidys that was meant to confirm the benefit behind its approval in older boys.

cellgene.why: Weakens the confirmatory evidence base for the most prominent AAV gene therapy in Duchenne.

pharma.why: Raises questions about how accelerated approvals get confirmed.

healthcare.why: Affects evidence available to families and payers for older boys.

e80e2ef0ae8e.summary: BioProcess International argues that UN biosecurity frameworks have not kept pace with how the biopharma industry has evolved.

biosecurity.why: Argues international biosecurity governance is out of date.

bioprocessing.why: Concerns oversight of biomanufacturing.

d7def69be5a6.summary: Immunocore says Kimmtrak brought in $102.2 million in Q3 2026 and $324.8 million over nine months, up 10% year on year.

pharma.why: Commercial track record of the first approved TCR bispecific.

investment.why: Steady revenue growth for a mid-cap biotech.

a135316ca550.summary: Candel presented three SITC posters, including a late-breaker, with clinical and biomarker data for its viral immunotherapy aglatimagene in prostate and lung cancer and linoserpaturev in glioblastoma, the company says.

cellgene.why: Adenoviral and HSV-based immunotherapies.

pharma.why: Supporting data rather than new pivotal results.

3508e4922a3d.summary: BioCardia says it has completed clinical consultation with Japan's PMDA for its CardiAMP cell therapy system and is moving towards a marketing approval application.

cellgene.why: Japan route for an autologous cardiac cell therapy.

meddevices.why: CardiAMP is a device-based cell delivery system.

622056b24b7c.summary: BioSpace previews a busy November of FDA decisions, including verdicts for Summit/Akeso, Capricor and Vertex.

pharma.why: Several high-profile FDA decisions due this month.

cellgene.why: Capricor's cell therapy is among them.

investment.why: Binary events for the companies involved.

c22af8c396d0.summary: Moderna posted its first profitable quarter in two years, with Q3 revenue of $1.3 billion driven by international Covid-19 vaccine sales, while it prioritises cancer vaccines.

pharma.why: Steadies the leading mRNA company's finances.

cellgene.why: Funds Moderna's mRNA cancer vaccine push.

investment.why: Beat analyst estimates and avoided a predicted loss.

7e07ede11905.summary: Science reports that Representative Zoe Lofgren, set to lead the House science committee after the Democrats' midterm win, and microbiologist Jasmine Clark outline a possible science agenda.

healthcare.why: Signals US research funding direction under a Democratic House.

pharma.why: Federal science policy affects biomedical research.

65b4a4a0cd15.summary: Science reports the first clinical result for a chemogenetic gene therapy: a team in China treated three people with epilepsy with a gene that lets a drug dampen brain cell activity, reducing seizures.

cellgene.why: First human use of drug-switchable gene therapy in the brain.

pharma.why: New approach for drug-resistant epilepsy.

decf446b0e40.summary: Nature reports an adhesive that binds strongly even underwater, inspired by a protein made by the cholera bacterium.

meddevices.why: Possible use in wet-tissue adhesives.

ec9682a7bd3b.summary: A preprint reports building genomic chimeras by expanding a genome at the megabase scale, combining genomic content from different organisms rather than only rebuilding existing genomes. Not yet peer-reviewed.

industrial.why: Megabase genome engineering for new organism functions.

tools.why: Large-scale genome synthesis method.

aa08943d58a5.summary: A preprint describes engineered living materials made of commensal bacteria that continuously secrete therapeutic proteins to help heal chronic wounds. Not yet peer-reviewed.

meddevices.why: Living-material wound dressing concept.

c1f1852b6096.summary: STAT reports that a sickle cell gene therapy previously abandoned could make a comeback; details are behind a paywall.

cellgene.why: Possible revival of a shelved sickle cell gene therapy.

a1791b921861.summary: Lilly and Hims & Hers say patients prescribed through the Hims & Hers platform can get Lilly's Zepbound (tirzepatide) and Foundayo (orforglipron) at self-pay prices starting at $299 and $149 a month. Hims & Hers committed never to offer compounded copies of Lilly's GLP-1 medicines.

pharma.why: Moves the leading obesity drugmaker's branded GLP-1s into the biggest telehealth channel that previously sold compounded copies.

healthcare.why: Shifts direct-to-consumer obesity care towards approved drugs at cash prices.

investment.why: Material for both companies' obesity revenue outlook.

34f0ff0c1608.summary: Madrigal Pharmaceuticals' former head of clinical development has filed a whistleblower lawsuit alleging senior leadership censored serious liver-injury data for its MASH drug Rezdiffra.

pharma.why: Safety allegations against the first approved MASH drug, now a blockbuster, could draw regulatory scrutiny.

investment.why: Litigation risk for Madrigal's single commercial product.

b2257b3e76cb.summary: CMS has formally codified the Medicare drug price negotiation framework set up under the Inflation Reduction Act, despite repeated industry challenges in court.

pharma.why: Locks in the process that sets Medicare prices for top-selling drugs, shaping revenue forecasts and pipeline choices.

healthcare.why: Sets how Medicare will pay for negotiated medicines.

investment.why: Reduces hope of the programme being unwound by regulation.

1d1866f390f7.summary: Green Queen reports the Good Food Institute laid off six US employees and eliminated seven more roles after a fall in its revenue.

agrifood.why: The leading alternative-protein think tank cutting staff signals tighter funding for the sector.

fermentation.why: GFI backs precision-fermentation research and advocacy.

4475ce3a5c19.summary: ScienceDaily reports a study finding psilocybin rapidly reshapes the brain by forming new neural connections and strengthening others.

pharma.why: Mechanistic support for psychedelic drug developers.

df0af3410900.summary: A preprint presents an open-source benchmark comparing sensory and functional properties of dairy and dairy-free products. Not yet peer-reviewed.

agrifood.why: Gives alt-dairy developers a shared way to measure how close products are to dairy.

fermentation.why: Relevant to precision-fermented dairy protein makers.

737b147c51bf.summary: A preprint maps human neutralizing antibodies against influenza in summer 2026, finding antigenic advance in H3N2 subclade K and H1N1 D.3.1.1 mutants, to inform vaccine strain updates. Not yet peer-reviewed.

pharma.why: Bears on which strains flu vaccine makers will need for the next season.

biosecurity.why: Near real-time immunity surveillance for drifting seasonal flu.

bcafdd10fcdf.summary: A preprint uses integrated omics to show how a toluene-degrading bacterium reorganises nitrogen and lipid metabolism when grown in the gas phase. Not yet peer-reviewed.

industrial.why: Informs gas-phase bioprocesses for converting poorly soluble compounds.

bioprocessing.why: Insight for designing immobilised-cell gas-phase reactors.

ac5474d8a025.summary: A preprint reports that R-pyocin selection restored aminoglycoside sensitivity in a pan-drug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolate. Not yet peer-reviewed.

pharma.why: A possible way to revive old antibiotics against the hardest resistant infections.

biosecurity.why: Relevant to antimicrobial resistance preparedness.

1da076445548.summary: ScienceDaily reports research suggesting a compound found naturally in broccoli could help treat Friedreich ataxia.

pharma.why: Early lead for a rare neurological disease with few treatments.

e2548616f447.summary: A Nature paper reports in vivo CRISPR base editing of ANGPTL3 that produced durable lipid lowering.

cellgene.why: One-time in vivo base editing for a common cardiovascular target is a key test case for gene editing beyond rare disease.

pharma.why: Points to a one-shot alternative to chronic lipid-lowering drugs.

7e4931900f76.summary: A preprint finds non-canonical peptidoglycan cross-linking is essential for Mycobacterium tuberculosis to resist acid inside macrophages. Not yet peer-reviewed.

pharma.why: Identifies a possible new target for TB drugs.

2e20b989713e.summary: The FDA said it is investigating a "serious risk" of cancer linked to Novartis's spinal muscular atrophy gene therapy Zolgensma and is weighing regulatory action on Zolgensma and Itvisma, a day after Novartis disclosed new tumour cases.

cellgene.why: A formal FDA safety probe into an approved AAV gene therapy could shape labels and vector-integration scrutiny across the field.

pharma.why: Regulatory action on Novartis's Zolgensma franchise affects a major commercial gene therapy.

healthcare.why: Families and clinicians treating SMA face new uncertainty about long-term tumour risk.

0aa79e991e54.summary: BIO and two California biotech trade groups sued in federal court in Northern California to halt GLOBE, the Medicare pilot that benchmarks drug prices to peer countries, arguing it oversteps Medicare's statutory authority. The pilot tests Trump's most-favoured-nation pricing approach, though its impact is expected to be limited.

pharma.why: The suit challenges a federal model that ties Medicare drug prices to international prices.

healthcare.why: The outcome affects how Medicare pays for drugs under the pilot.

investment.why: Investors track legal challenges to international reference pricing as a drug-revenue risk.

8c9a6d8b2ff4.summary: NYU Langone says ISCHEMIA-EXTEND, following more than 5,000 patients with stable coronary disease for up to 13 years, found early invasive procedures gave no survival advantage over drug therapy (about 26% vs 27% died). Presented at AHA and published in JAMA.

healthcare.why: Long-term evidence that routine stenting or bypass does not extend life in stable heart disease bears on standard care.

meddevices.why: It weakens the case for routine use of stents and other invasive cardiology procedures in stable patients.

pharma.why: It supports medical therapy as the first-line approach.

e0888a81a916.summary: J&J says its oral IL-23 receptor peptide Icotyde (icotrokinra) gave ACR20 responses in 58% and ACR50 in 29% of biologic-naive psoriatic arthritis patients at week 16 in a phase 3 study presented at ACR.

pharma.why: Phase 3 data extend J&J's first-in-class oral IL-23R peptide from psoriasis into psoriatic arthritis, a large immunology market.

healthcare.why: A daily pill could offer an alternative to injected biologics for psoriatic arthritis.

5bce5e5bfb83.summary: J&J presented patient-experience data at ACR from its phase 2 nipocalimab study in Sjögren's disease, showing mouth dryness was the symptom patients most wanted improved; the company cites a 50% increase in saliva production in the trial.

pharma.why: Supports J&J's FcRn blocker nipocalimab as it moves through development in Sjögren's disease.

healthcare.why: Highlights which Sjögren's symptoms matter most to patients.

5e2f116d582e.summary: argenx says efgartigimod beat placebo in the phase 3 ALKIVIA trial in idiopathic inflammatory myopathy, with mean Total Improvement Score 48.0 vs 32.6 at week 52 (p=0.0011); it plans an FDA filing for immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy by end-2026, while the dermatomyositis subgroup was not significant.

pharma.why: Opens a new indication for the FcRn blocker Vyvgart in a myositis market with few targeted options.

healthcare.why: Could give patients with necrotizing myopathy an approved targeted therapy.

7b6ab0097c4d.summary: On his first earnings call, Sarepta CEO Michael Severino reported $83.5 million in Q3 Elevidys sales (down from $131.5 million a year earlier), said ENVISION enrolment will not resume and expects market share erosion from 2H 2027 as Dyne's and Regenxbio's Duchenne therapies near the market.

cellgene.why: Falling sales of the leading Duchenne gene therapy and new competition reshape the DMD gene therapy market.

pharma.why: Sarepta's outlook and pipeline shift towards siRNA programmes from Arrowhead.

investment.why: Analysts are watching whether Elevidys sales stabilise before competitors launch.

0dc3dcf79e97.summary: Researchers describe a microfluidic sieve and detector that processes 200 microlitres in one minute and quantifies biomarkers at single-molecule sensitivity, aiming to cut ultrasensitive assay time from hours to minutes. Not yet peer-reviewed.

diagnostics.why: Much faster ultrasensitive assays could bring single-molecule biomarker tests closer to point of care.

tools.why: A new microfluidic platform for rapid low-abundance protein detection.

becd505e589e.summary: MIT researchers used ligand-directed lipid nanoparticles carrying mRNA to turn natural killer cells into CAR-NK cells inside the body, clearing T cell lymphoma in humanised mice after five injections, putting 3 of 5 mice with melanoma into remission and healing autoimmune hepatitis in mice; published in Nature Biotechnology.

cellgene.why: In vivo CAR-NK engineering with mRNA nanoparticles could remove ex vivo cell manufacturing.

pharma.why: It adds to in vivo CAR approaches for cancer and autoimmune disease.

bioprocessing.why: In vivo engineering would bypass cell therapy manufacturing.

20ccb2c8ad8f.summary: STAT's Matthew Herper argues that the AHA failures of Novartis's pelacarsen and Novo Nordisk's ziltivekimab, both backed by human genetics, show that hyped technologies promising faster drug development, AI included, can still fall flat.

pharma.why: It questions how far genetic validation de-risks cardiovascular drug targets.

ai.why: It cautions against assuming AI will raise drug development success rates.

investment.why: It challenges a common investment thesis for AI and genetics-led biotechs.

100bfe54c385.summary: NEJM published a randomised trial of intensive versus standard blood-pressure lowering in patients with type 2 diabetes, presented at AHA 2026; results are not visible in the feed.

healthcare.why: Blood-pressure targets for people with diabetes drive treatment guidelines.

pharma.why: Tighter targets would raise use of antihypertensive drugs.

de7d4bc706c7.summary: NEJM published a randomised trial of intensive versus standard blood-pressure control in patients with a previous ischaemic stroke, presented at AHA 2026; results are not visible in the feed.

healthcare.why: It informs blood-pressure targets for secondary stroke prevention.

pharma.why: Tighter targets would raise use of antihypertensive drugs.

41784520c588.summary: NEJM published a randomised trial of stopping statins in older adults without cardiovascular disease, presented at AHA 2026; results are not visible in the feed.

healthcare.why: It bears on deprescribing statins in a large older population.

pharma.why: It could change long-term statin use in older patients.

74efa911c983.summary: NEJM published a trial of starting extracorporeal life support before hospital arrival in refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, with an accompanying editorial on bringing rapid reperfusion to more patients; results are not visible in the feed.

healthcare.why: It tests whether emergency services should deliver ECMO in the field.

meddevices.why: Prehospital ECMO depends on portable extracorporeal devices.

fa299b7eef87.summary: Full Lp(a)HORIZON results in NEJM, presented at AHA, showed Novartis's pelacarsen sharply lowered Lp(a) but did not reduce heart attacks, strokes, urgent revascularisation or deaths versus placebo over almost five years.

pharma.why: The first Lp(a) outcomes trial failing raises doubts over Amgen's and Lilly's late-stage Lp(a) drugs.

cellgene.why: Pelacarsen is an antisense drug, and the readout weighs on RNA-targeting cardiovascular programmes.

investment.why: Investors will reprice the Lp(a) class ahead of Amgen and Lilly readouts.

healthcare.why: It undercuts lowering Lp(a) as a proven route to fewer cardiovascular events.

a6d6ddac6cda.summary: Full ZEUS results in NEJM, presented at AHA, showed Novo Nordisk's IL-6 antibody ziltivekimab had almost no effect on cardiovascular events despite hitting its target, after the July topline miss cut Novo's shares 9%.

pharma.why: A null phase 3 for IL-6 blockade hits Novo's cardiovascular pipeline and the wider anti-inflammatory heart drug strategy.

healthcare.why: It leaves inflammation-targeted prevention for patients with atherosclerosis and kidney disease unproven.

investment.why: It weighs on valuations of companies developing IL-6 and other inflammation drugs for heart disease.

dabc4c3d7b09.summary: Antengene says preclinical data at SITC 2026 for its AnTenGager-D2 costimulatory T cell engager platform showed potent tumour killing with limited off-target T cell activation, led by ATG-109 (KLK2 x CD2 x CD3) for prostate cancer. Animal and cell data only.

pharma.why: Adds a CD2-costimulated design to the crowded T cell engager field, still preclinical.

7d57513f88df.summary: Immutep says a late-breaking ACR 2026 abstract showed its first-in-class LAG-3 agonist antibody IMP761 produced statistically significant, exposure-dependent inhibition of T-cell-driven immune responses in a phase 1 study.

pharma.why: Early human evidence for LAG-3 agonism as a new route to dampen autoimmune T cells.

a3d82e34179a.summary: Mineralys says lorundrostat kept office systolic blood pressure 17.8 mmHg below baseline at week 48 in the Transform-HTN open-label extension, which it calls the largest long-term trial of an aldosterone synthase inhibitor, presented at AHA 2026.

pharma.why: Durability data for a drug class (aldosterone synthase inhibitors) competing for resistant hypertension.

healthcare.why: Hypertension is common and often uncontrolled despite current drugs.

7c006886f98e.summary: Vir Biotechnology's once-monthly tobevibart plus elebsiran met its primary endpoints in ECLIPSE 1, the first of three pivotal chronic hepatitis D trials, with 44% of patients reaching undetectable virus at week 48. It sets up competition with Gilead's Hepcludex and Mirum's brelovitug.

pharma.why: First pivotal win for an antibody plus siRNA combination in hepatitis D, a disease with few options.

investment.why: A key de-risking event for Vir and a read on the hepatitis D market.

0452c30bba10.summary: Novo Nordisk says a post hoc analysis presented at AASLD 2026 found semaglutide 2.4 mg improved liver injury, fibrosis and disease activity measures at week 72 versus placebo in adults with MASH and liver scarring whose BMI was below 27.

pharma.why: Supports Wegovy's MASH use beyond obesity, though only as a post hoc subgroup.

470cf47ba396.summary: Johnson & Johnson says its dual-antigen regimen of two bispecifics, pasritamig (KLK2) and JNJ-9401 (PSMA), produced a 73% PSA response rate with every-six-week dosing in an early study in advanced prostate cancer.

pharma.why: Early sign that combining two T cell engagers can work in prostate cancer, a hard target for immunotherapy.

d0720303897b.summary: Its developer says the BCMAxCD3 T cell engager velinotamig improved disease activity in 8 of 9 evaluable patients with systemic lupus erythematosus, with complete renal responses, in data presented at ACR 2026.

pharma.why: Adds to evidence that T cell engagers can reset autoimmune disease, rivalling CAR-T in lupus.

14f79cbfcb16.summary: CRISPR Therapeutics says 5 of 6 systemic sclerosis patients given its allogeneic CAR-T zugo-cel with standard lymphodepletion had a clinical response at month 3, and all responders kept it, in data presented at ACR 2026.

cellgene.why: Off-the-shelf CAR-T in autoimmune disease is one of the most watched cell therapy bets.

pharma.why: Competition for B cell reset therapies in scleroderma and lupus.

33916032645c.summary: A placebo-controlled randomised trial in Nature Medicine, presented at AHA 2026, found semaglutide significantly improved pulmonary artery wedge pressure and other haemodynamics during exercise in obese patients with HFpEF; a companion MRI substudy of CAMEO-SEMA showed improved cardiac structure and function.

pharma.why: Mechanistic evidence for why GLP-1 drugs help HFpEF, supporting the label expansion.

healthcare.why: HFpEF with obesity is common and has few effective treatments.

0e3b045175b7.summary: Daewoong Pharmaceutical signed joint development agreements for two drug-delivery platforms from affiliate Daewoong Therapeutics: Thermicra, for turning intravenous biologics into subcutaneous forms, and a dissolving microneedle platform.

pharma.why: Subcutaneous conversion of IV biologics is a lifecycle tool for biologic drugs.

meddevices.why: Dissolving microneedles are a device-like delivery format.

2916dce6c5c6.summary: A nationwide Korean study led by CHA University Bundang Medical Center found that better regional sepsis care could substantially cut deaths, and called sepsis a priority for emergency care policy.

healthcare.why: Argues for organising sepsis care as a national system.

2fb1a4e4b6dd.summary: Gilead has renewed its bid for second-line Korean reimbursement of the CAR-T Yescarta in DLBCL, while Curocell prepares a second-line trial of its domestic CAR-T Rimqarto that could widen patient access.

cellgene.why: Covers CAR-T access and reimbursement in a key Asian market.

healthcare.why: Reimbursement decides who gets CAR-T in Korea.

972fbea98f93.summary: Celltrion says the EMA's CHMP recommended extending its Stelara biosimilar Steqeyma (ustekinumab) to Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis in children aged two and older.

pharma.why: Paediatric label extension for a major ustekinumab biosimilar in the EU.

c01f379b3e71.summary: More than 60% of Korean children with solid tumours are now enrolled in a national precision medicine platform funded by a 300 billion won ($200 million) donation from the late Samsung chairman's family, according to Seoul National University Hospital.

healthcare.why: National-scale precision oncology programme for paediatric cancer.

diagnostics.why: Built on genomic profiling of tumours.

c9b9c587176e.summary: Peptron says Mexico's COFEPRIS approved LUPUNIA, its once-monthly leuprorelin injection for prostate cancer and precocious puberty, on bioequivalence to the original product.

pharma.why: Generic long-acting leuprorelin approval in Latin America.

30849f61a197.summary: At the Politzer Society meeting, experts said gene therapy for hereditary hearing loss is showing hearing gains but cautioned about limited eligibility, uncertain long-term safety and continued need for rehabilitation.

cellgene.why: Expert view on the emerging otoferlin-type gene therapies for deafness.

18f711611536.summary: Sky Labs signed an MOU with Abu Dhabi's SEHA Clinics, part of PureHealth, to evaluate its CART BP ring blood pressure monitor in clinical settings in the UAE.

meddevices.why: Clinical evaluation of a wearable cuffless BP monitor abroad.

8b365cda67e1.summary: Kyorin Pharmaceutical is paying $12 million upfront, in a deal worth up to about $140 million, for Japan rights to Edesa Biotech's phase 3 anti-TLR4 antibody for acute respiratory distress syndrome.

pharma.why: Regional licensing of a late-stage ARDS antibody.

investment.why: Non-dilutive funding for a small-cap biotech.

3e64b8d8ed08.summary: Faeth Therapeutics says its oral combination therapy for endometrial cancer cleared its phase 2 efficacy bar, and it will push ahead in a field dominated by injectable ADCs.

pharma.why: Oral challenger in an endometrial cancer market targeted by big ADC programmes.

c845bd57ed92.summary: Valneva and LimmaTech's tetravalent Shigella vaccine S4V2 reduced intestinal infections and hit the key endpoint in a phase 2 controlled human infection trial, alongside infant safety and immunogenicity data.

pharma.why: Shigella has no licensed vaccine; this is a leading candidate.

healthcare.why: Shigella is a major cause of child diarrhoeal deaths in low-income countries.

biosecurity.why: Vaccine against an enteric pathogen with rising antimicrobial resistance.

433e1288b6db.summary: Argenx will acquire Unnatural Products, a macrocycle peptide biotech partnered with Merck and Novartis, for $550 million upfront in cash plus contingent value rights, up to about $1.15 billion in total, to add oral peptide discovery to its immunology business.

pharma.why: Argenx's biggest buy, aimed at oral alternatives to its injected antibodies.

investment.why: Billion-dollar private biotech exit.

tools.why: Acquires a peptide discovery platform.

7935eb16050f.summary: Aisa Pharma says AISA-021 significantly reduced weekly Raynaud's attack frequency and duration versus placebo in the phase 2 RECONNOITER-1 trial in systemic sclerosis, with data due at ACR Convergence 2026.

pharma.why: Phase 2 data in an underserved rheumatology indication.

6f4e91c45788.summary: Eilean Therapeutics says a single oral dose of its MALT1 degrader ZE66-0205 cut MALT1 by 57% in healthy volunteers, the first human MALT1 degradation, with no adverse findings in three-month primate toxicology.

pharma.why: First clinical proof of mechanism for a MALT1 degrader.

08c1b1841f19.summary: Adneuris Therapeutics submitted an NDA to the FDA for cebranopadol in moderate-to-severe acute pain; it says the drug would be the first dual NOP/MOP receptor agonist painkiller if approved.

pharma.why: New analgesic mechanism filing in a market seeking opioid alternatives.

healthcare.why: Acute pain treatment options beyond classic opioids.

32c74d5a7801.summary: BioVie says biomarkers from its phase 2 ADDRESS-LC trial of bezisterim suggest two Long COVID endotypes with different treatment responses, presented at an NIH RECOVER-TLC workshop.

pharma.why: Exploratory biomarker data in Long COVID.

2b78a94ec763.summary: Humacyte has started a first-in-human study of its acellular engineered vessel as a coronary artery bypass conduit and is about to begin screening patients.

meddevices.why: Bioengineered vessel moving into cardiac surgery.

cellgene.why: Tissue-engineered product grown from human cells.

8cb4b02dd465.summary: STAT reports that Trump administration officials issued new guidelines meant to stop AI-enabled design tools from helping bad actors create bioweapons. Details are behind STAT's paywall.

biosecurity.why: New US federal guidance on AI-enabled bioweapon risk.

ai.why: Targets AI tools used for biological design.

defence.why: Bioweapon prevention is a national security issue.

b680b3cfce60.summary: NAMSA and Advanced Medical Solutions announced a preferred partnership under which NAMSA will provide testing, biological safety, regulatory and clinical research services for AMS's tissue-healing products.

meddevices.why: Medtech CRO partnership for wound and tissue-healing devices.

514031374e84.summary: Biond Biologics dosed the first patient with BND-67, an anti-CD28 shedding antibody intended to boost anti-tumour T-cell activity, first alone and then with an anti-PD-1.

pharma.why: New immuno-oncology mechanism entering the clinic.

d54306471abb.summary: PharmAla Biotech will supply MDMA to Aalborg University Hospital for a Danish randomised trial of MDMA-assisted treatment for service-related PTSD, in exchange for cash and trial data.

pharma.why: Psychedelic-assisted therapy trial in Europe.

892101e3b925.summary: Bengaluru biomaterials startup AltM, founded by former Tesla staff, raised $10.3 million to scale technology that converts agricultural waste into bio-based ingredients for cosmetics, packaging and textiles.

industrial.why: Scaling bio-based materials from crop residue.

agrifood.why: Upcycles farm waste.

investment.why: Venture round for Indian industrial biotech.

985b20251dee.summary: Hemab Therapeutics started SOLARA, a pivotal phase 3 trial of once-weekly subcutaneous sutacimig in about 75 people with Glanzmann thrombasthenia, a rare bleeding disorder with no approved preventive therapy.

pharma.why: First pivotal trial for a prophylactic in this rare bleeding disorder.

b67d0b0c6707.summary: Editas Medicine reported Q3 results and received Australian ethics approval to start the phase 1/2 Strive study of its in vivo gene editing candidate EDIT-401 for hyperlipidemia.

cellgene.why: In vivo LDLR-targeted gene editing heading to the clinic.

f32d48d65787.summary: Nkarta reported initial clinical data at ACR Convergence for its CD19 CAR-NK cell therapy NKX019 in myositis and systemic sclerosis.

cellgene.why: Allogeneic CAR-NK in autoimmune disease, part of the cell-therapy reset trend.

pharma.why: Autoimmune pipeline data.

a714c0a009b4.summary: Bloomberg reports that Johnson & Johnson backed a psychedelic-inspired biotech in a $100 million financing round.

pharma.why: Big pharma money into next-generation psychedelic-derived drugs.

investment.why: Nine-figure private round.

d5c957acb4a5.summary: Researchers found that gut bacteria starved of fibre feed on the intestinal mucus lining and make potentially harmful compounds, while fibre and plant proteins steer them toward beneficial metabolites.

agrifood.why: Mechanistic case for fibre in diet and food design.

healthcare.why: Microbiome link to gut barrier health.

0a904233ad36.summary: Vaxcellbio says its dual-target CAR-T VCB-1204 produced complete responses in all animals in a liver cancer model, in preclinical data presented at SITC 2026.

cellgene.why: Preclinical CAR-T for solid tumours.

ee2a7cbce449.summary: An Asan Medical Center study found AI assistance improved doctors' accuracy in diagnosing middle ear disease from endoscopic images, with junior trainees gaining 32.2 percentage points.

ai.why: Clinical evidence for AI decision support in imaging.

ff96022f7e79.summary: A 35-year study found mouse populations, boosted by acorn crops, drive Lyme disease risk more than deer, with mice fuelling a 40% rise in tick numbers the following year.

biosecurity.why: Better forecasting of tick-borne disease risk.

healthcare.why: Informs Lyme disease prevention.

d27a63a451ab.summary: Samsung Bioepis says its proposed Keytruda biosimilar SB27 met phase 3 equivalence in metastatic NSCLC, with a week-24 response rate of 34.6% versus 37.9% for Keytruda.

pharma.why: Positions one of the first pembrolizumab biosimilars ahead of Keytruda patent expiry.

bioprocessing.why: Biosimilar manufacturing competition.

b4625a7a7d70.summary: STAT examines whether AI chatbots, though imperfect therapists, could help men who avoid traditional mental health care to open up.

ai.why: AI in mental health support.

healthcare.why: Access to mental health care for men.

561bb208a4a0.summary: The UK MHRA awarded Innovation Passports under its ILAP pathway to Alnylam's siRNA brezosiran for Huntington's disease, BeOne's PRMT5 inhibitor BGB-58067 for NSCLC and Biogen's antisense diranersen for early Alzheimer's.

pharma.why: Faster UK route for three late-stage neuro and oncology drugs.

cellgene.why: Two are oligonucleotide (RNA) medicines.

0ed73982a85d.summary: BioProcess International's second part argues that better analytics and new modalities justify rethinking how biosimilars and other biologics are developed, with lighter clinical requirements.

bioprocessing.why: Analytical-led biosimilar development.

pharma.why: Biosimilar regulatory thinking.

48fa53a56be3.summary: GENFIT highlighted data from earlier studies of nangibotide, a TREM-1 inhibitor, backing its move into acute-on-chronic liver failure, with phase 2 data expected in 2027.

pharma.why: Pipeline update in a liver disease with no approved therapy.

d90d13b945d6.summary: UCB and Biogen say dapirolizumab pegol produced higher lupus treatment response rates than placebo using a new response measure, in analyses presented at ACR 2026.

pharma.why: Supports a late-stage lupus biologic heading to filing.
