e7442b30ff5e.summary: An analysis suggests plant-based meat and legumes in India can deliver comparable or higher bioavailable protein than meat, an opening for plant protein makers.

agrifood.why: Protein quality case for plant-based foods in India.

0fc7db3fb480.summary: Researchers found that build-up of the mitochondrial protein Miro1 may drive insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes; removing it restored muscle insulin response in preclinical work, and exercise lowered Miro1 in people.

pharma.why: Possible new target in insulin resistance.

62ae8b1c56f0.summary: GlycoNex filed its denosumab biosimilar SPD8 with Japan's PMDA, with a decision expected as early as end-2027, and is seeking partners outside Japan.

pharma.why: Another denosumab biosimilar entering Japan.

14b548b754bf.summary: A Nature editorial warns the developing super El Niño is a health shock as well as a climate one, with food shortages and disease outbreaks expected, and calls for them to be tackled together.

biosecurity.why: Anticipates climate-driven outbreaks.

healthcare.why: Public health preparedness.

agrifood.why: Food shortages from El Niño.

25ceb6beb032.summary: UCSF scientists engineered B-SYNC CAR-T cells that switch on only in the brain; they eliminated diffuse midline glioma in every mouse tested.

cellgene.why: Tissue-gated CAR-T design for lethal paediatric brain tumours.

pharma.why: Preclinical oncology.

38f171fe8d85.summary: An NEJM trial tested community and emergency medical service interventions to improve survival after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest.

healthcare.why: Evidence on how to organise cardiac arrest response.

11fb62734eb1.summary: An NEJM trial compared left bundle-branch pacing with conventional right ventricular pacing in patients with atrioventricular block.

meddevices.why: Head-to-head evidence on pacemaker lead placement.

healthcare.why: Affects standard pacing practice.

54189a74bdb2.summary: NEJM published a trial of Lilly's once-weekly retatrutide in adults with knee osteoarthritis pain and obesity.

pharma.why: Extends the triple agonist into osteoarthritis pain.

healthcare.why: Obesity-related joint disease is common.

681d9c269d1c.summary: FDA approved Bayer's Sunharbo (asundexian) 50 mg, the first factor XIa inhibitor, for use with antiplatelet therapy to cut stroke risk after a recent mild-to-moderate non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk TIA.

pharma.why: First US approval in the factor XIa class, long seen as a route to anticoagulation with less bleeding.

healthcare.why: Adds a new secondary stroke-prevention option for neurologists and stroke services.

a717513366a3.summary: Veradermics reported 12-month phase 3 data for its oral minoxidil in men with hair loss, its best hair-growth results of the programme so far, with solid one-year safety.

pharma.why: Late-stage readout that completes the phase 3 programme ahead of a filing in androgenetic alopecia.

3dd298289b13.summary: Merck said its GLP-1/glucagon co-agonist efinopegdutide resolved MASH versus placebo without worsening liver fibrosis in a mid-stage trial.

pharma.why: Supports a big-pharma incretin entrant in the competitive MASH field.

6bf6f8fa099c.summary: Ionis lost more than $1 billion in market value on Monday after cutting sales projections for its triglyceride-lowering drug on a slow launch.

pharma.why: A weak launch for a newly approved RNA-targeted cardiometabolic drug.

investment.why: Large one-day market-value loss for a mid-cap biotech.

9153567c1c4f.summary: Illumina opened an early access programme for a duplex sequencing workflow that reads both DNA strands to detect trace ctDNA for minimal residual disease and tumour evolution research.

tools.why: New sequencing workflow from the market leader aimed at low-frequency variant detection.

diagnostics.why: Targets MRD research that feeds liquid-biopsy diagnostics.

c909424a47c8.summary: Coherus Oncology reported Q3 results and a strategic prioritisation plan that focuses development on tagmokitug with toripalimab in esophageal cancer, with plans for expedited development.

pharma.why: Pipeline narrowing at a small oncology company toward one lead combination.

69ff7e49a1ae.summary: GEN reports a study showing the cancer-associated transcription factor E2F1 can trigger cell division without unpacking chromatin, using a shortcut pathway.

pharma.why: Basic cell-cycle biology relevant to cancer drug targets.

65e16bde2766.summary: Larimar Therapeutics completed its rolling BLA seeking accelerated approval of nomlabofusp for Friedreich's ataxia.

pharma.why: A rare neurological disease filing that would add a second Friedreich's ataxia therapy.

9b4925183e31.summary: PharmaLogic agreed to buy Lantheus' CDMO business and its Springfield, New Jersey manufacturing site, which it says creates the first transatlantic CDMO with a commercial record in radioligand therapies. Terms not in the excerpt.

bioprocessing.why: Consolidates scarce radiopharmaceutical manufacturing capacity.

pharma.why: Radioligand developers depend on this kind of specialised CDMO capacity.

6ee28da3aa7f.summary: Oruka says its ORKA-001 high-dose group reached 61% PASI 100 and 86% PASI 90 at week 16 in the EVERLAST-B psoriasis study, consistent with EVERLAST-A.

pharma.why: Strong skin-clearance data for a long-acting IL-23 antibody in a crowded psoriasis market.

c71b36801a65.summary: Teams in ARPA-H's Advocate programme for autonomous clinical AI have already held an initial informational meeting with FDA, less than two months after launch, according to the programme manager.

ai.why: Early signal of how FDA will approach autonomous clinical AI tools.

healthcare.why: Autonomous AI agents could change clinical workflows.

meddevices.why: Such tools would likely be regulated as software medical devices.

eb22f4613543.summary: CDMO Simtra BioPharma Solutions opened a new sterile injectable manufacturing building in Bloomington, Indiana, a $250+ million expansion.

bioprocessing.why: Adds US fill-finish capacity for injectables.

pharma.why: More onshore sterile manufacturing for drugmakers.

9ce0766b2911.summary: Endpoints reports that companies that signed Trump's most-favoured-nation drug pricing deals now face hard choices on where and when to launch new medicines, since US prices are tied to those charged abroad.

pharma.why: MFN commitments shape global launch sequencing and pricing for new drugs.

healthcare.why: Could delay launches in lower-priced markets.

7e8f29071e0a.summary: FDA told GLP-1 drugmakers to add label warnings about an increased risk of a rare eye condition that can lead to blindness.

pharma.why: Class-wide label change for the biggest-selling drug class.

healthcare.why: Affects prescribing and patient counselling for millions on GLP-1s.

09eb40ea1e9f.summary: CDMO Curia expanded fermentation capacity at its site in León, Spain.

fermentation.why: More microbial fermentation capacity in Europe.

bioprocessing.why: CDMO capacity expansion for fermentation-derived APIs.

a64723aee7da.summary: The Pentagon removed WuXi AppTec from its list of Chinese military companies, though Endpoints notes the Shanghai CRDMO still risks being redesignated.

pharma.why: Eases pressure on a key outsourcing partner used across the industry.

bioprocessing.why: Affects US-China manufacturing supply chains and Biosecure-style decoupling.

defence.why: A Department of Defense designation decision on a biotech supplier.

70d1bb95f7af.summary: Third Rock Ventures agreed a research collaboration worth up to $2.16 billion with Funnel Biosciences, a little-known Chinese biotech that describes itself as an AI-driven biologics company focused on antibody discovery.

ai.why: A large bet on an AI antibody-discovery platform.

investment.why: A top US venture firm sourcing assets from China at scale.

pharma.why: Adds to the flow of China-originated biologics into Western pipelines.

dae2743ad09a.summary: Moderna is moving its UK commercial base to London's 'knowledge quarter', Fierce Pharma reports.

pharma.why: Signals Moderna's continued commitment to its UK partnership.

3dbc135c8a06.summary: J&J's oral IL-23 pill Icotyde showed strong phase 3 efficacy in biologic-naive psoriatic arthritis, but a high dose missed statistical significance on the primary endpoint.

pharma.why: Tests whether an oral peptide can match injectable biologics in a second indication.

b2b2b2114b70.summary: Sanofi-backed Windward Bio set terms for an IPO targeting about $204 million to fund two respiratory drugs licensed from China.

investment.why: Another sizeable biotech IPO in a reopening window.

pharma.why: China-licensed respiratory assets moving toward US markets.

3591e7378231.summary: Zura Bio's tibulizumab failed a phase 2 trial in hidradenitis suppurativa; the company is ending development in that indication and its stock sank.

pharma.why: A setback for dual IL-17/BAFF targeting in a competitive inflammatory skin disease.

4e624da0b268.summary: Spruce Biosciences spun out a preclinical endocrinology programme into a newly formed subsidiary, Adrenyx Biosciences.

pharma.why: Small restructuring of an early endocrinology asset.

331a81ac8665.summary: Boehringer Ingelheim plans to file survodutide for obesity in 2027 after a phase 3 study presented at AHA met its cardiovascular safety test.

pharma.why: Adds another incretin-class obesity drug heading to regulators.

healthcare.why: More competition in obesity treatment could affect access and pricing.

3ca125a33d2c.summary: Marea Therapeutics said MAR001 significantly cut blood triglycerides in the first part of a phase 2b study in hypertriglyceridemia, presented at AHA after its merger with Lisata.

pharma.why: Mid-stage lipid data in a field crowded with RNA and gene-editing approaches.

c659b9e2a848.summary: Delix Therapeutics raised a $100 million series C, backed by investors including Johnson & Johnson, to advance a phase 2-ready non-hallucinatory psychedelic-derived drug for depression.

pharma.why: Funds a neuroplastogen approach that avoids hallucinogenic effects.

investment.why: Sizeable private round in psychiatry with pharma backing.

5e94c9f9c1d2.summary: Onchilles says its intratumoral therapeutic N17350 cleared lesions distant from the injected tumour in early solid-tumour data.

pharma.why: Early evidence of an abscopal effect for a novel intratumoral approach.

09967534f4ea.summary: Labcorp completed its $375 million takeover of Millennium Health, including $245 million upfront, expanding its drug-testing business.

diagnostics.why: Consolidation in US clinical lab testing.

healthcare.why: Wider reach for drug-monitoring tests.

a5d68163313d.summary: GenomeWeb reports on PATHFINDER, a project to deliver point-of-care tests for infectious diseases in Africa.

diagnostics.why: Point-of-care infectious disease testing for low-resource settings.

biosecurity.why: Better local diagnosis strengthens outbreak detection in Africa.

537eb7b7edd0.summary: A study analyses patents to map biosafety trends in synthetic biology.

biosecurity.why: Tracks how biosafety features are being built into synthetic biology inventions.

8552ce0917bd.summary: FDA rejected Novocure's Tumor Treating Fields for brain metastases, citing uncertainty about the degree of clinical benefit, the company said.

meddevices.why: A rejection for a device-based cancer therapy's expansion.

healthcare.why: Limits options for patients with brain metastases.

6dfa413be7bf.summary: The UK MHRA updated its guidance on the Innovative Licensing and Access Pathway (ILAP), its route for speeding transformative medicines to UK patients.

pharma.why: Guidance for companies using the UK's fast-track pathway.

b6738d9723c4.summary: CorMedix is buying Heron Therapeutics' assets for $145 million upfront, in an Endpoints roundup that also covers Faeth's stock fall and news from Immunovant, Abeona and others.

pharma.why: Consolidation among small commercial-stage specialty pharma companies.

e46e49330418.summary: FDA published a discussion paper and invited public comment as it shapes policy for telesurgery and robotic medical devices with autonomous functions.

meddevices.why: Early regulatory framing for autonomous and remote surgical robots.

ai.why: Covers autonomy in AI-driven devices.

40edee44a394.summary: BioPharma Dive recounts how a failed pivotal Alzheimer's trial tied to Vivek Ramaswamy's biotech career followed his political run.

investment.why: Background on a high-profile biotech founder's record.

6a8c5f984524.summary: Hinge Bio presented healthy-volunteer safety and B-cell depletion data for HB2198 in autoimmune disease at ACR Convergence 2026.

pharma.why: Early data in the busy B-cell depletion for autoimmunity space.

b5a195caf95e.summary: Kraig Labs says it is shipping its spider silk to developers in performance apparel and advanced materials.

industrial.why: Commercial sampling of a bio-based engineered material.

7738b4e72032.summary: FoodNavigator examines when biomanufacturing will deliver on its promise to transform food production.

agrifood.why: Assesses the commercial timeline for bio-made food ingredients.

fermentation.why: Precision fermentation scale-up is central to the question.

430a309bda32.summary: STAT reports that a small number of tumour cases now offer strong evidence that viral vectors used in gene therapy can cause cancer, a risk debated for years.

cellgene.why: Directly concerns the safety of AAV and other viral-vector gene therapies.

pharma.why: May raise regulatory scrutiny across gene therapy programmes.

00e98a1f3070.summary: Eli Lilly's oral GLP-1 Foundayo reduced obstructive sleep apnea severity in phase 3 data at AHA, and Lilly plans to seek approval in the indication; STAT notes it looked less effective than Lilly's injectable.

pharma.why: Expands the label race between Lilly and Novo in obesity-related disease.

healthcare.why: A pill option for sleep apnea could widen treatment.

a2d423100dfc.summary: CRISPR Therapeutics says one-time gene-editing therapy CTX310 lowered ANGPTL3 and triglycerides in patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia in phase 1b data presented as an AHA late-breaker.

cellgene.why: In vivo gene editing advancing into common cardiovascular disease.

pharma.why: Competes with RNA drugs for lipid lowering.

43cb19f90bcd.summary: A review suggests childhood cancers may spread through developmental plasticity rather than needing extra mutations.

pharma.why: Conceptual input for paediatric oncology drug targeting.

15da096b96a1.summary: GEN reviews how new AI models are moving computer-designed protein therapeutics from proof of concept to wet-lab validation and clinical trials.

ai.why: Overview of AI protein design reaching the clinic.

pharma.why: De novo designed proteins are entering drug pipelines.

8fc4090dfaaa.summary: Werewolf Therapeutics presented clinical data for its conditionally activated cytokines WTX-124 and WTX-330 at SITC 2026.

pharma.why: Early data for masked cytokine immunotherapies.

f71b5e0b3aa3.summary: Pliant Therapeutics presented preclinical and clinical data for PLN-101095 at SITC 2026.

pharma.why: Early oncology data from a company pivoting after a fibrosis setback.

7be3c2fe32ab.summary: Science reports findings that AI outperformed scientists at spotting technical errors in clinical research papers.

ai.why: Shows AI can strengthen peer review of medical research.

healthcare.why: Better error detection in studies that drive medical decisions.

6bdd0b4410e5.summary: The US government imposed new rules on ordering synthetic DNA to deter bioterrorism; Science reports biosecurity experts gave the policy tempered praise.

biosecurity.why: Federal screening rules for synthetic DNA orders are a core biosecurity safeguard.

tools.why: DNA synthesis providers and their customers must comply.

industrial.why: Synthetic biology companies rely on synthetic DNA orders.

fa56d51dd3f1.summary: Preprint profiling porcine epidemic diarrhea virus transcription and translation finds noncanonical RNA junctions and hidden coding potential. Not yet peer-reviewed.

agrifood.why: PEDV is a major threat to the swine industry.

c97d8cce3a49.summary: Preprint finds diverse bacteria grow more than additively on mixtures of different classes of carbon sources. Not yet peer-reviewed.

fermentation.why: Could inform feedstock design for microbial fermentation.

2f1b51b89063.summary: Preprint reports citrate-based hydrogels promoted closure of infected diabetic wounds. Not yet peer-reviewed.

meddevices.why: Candidate wound-care biomaterial for diabetic foot ulcers.

d06c07b2ee67.summary: Preprint describes a low-cost, scalable pipette-driven microfluidic platform for formulating lipid nanoparticles. Not yet peer-reviewed.

tools.why: Accessible LNP formulation method for labs.

cellgene.why: LNPs deliver mRNA and gene-editing medicines.

bioprocessing.why: Relevant to small-scale LNP process development.

9d6b52346a0b.summary: Preprint finds mitochondrial transplantation redirects rather than suppresses the inflammatory response of primary human monocytes. Not yet peer-reviewed.

pharma.why: Early mechanistic data on an experimental immunomodulation approach.

40639fc23f84.summary: A Nature Medicine analysis of patient-reported response trajectories to vedolizumab defines ulcerative colitis endotypes and points to vascular inflammation as a possible resistance mechanism.

pharma.why: Could guide patient stratification and new targets in IBD.

healthcare.why: Supports more personalised UC treatment.

230e7e657a55.summary: In a Nature Medicine randomised trial, people doing resistance exercise while on tirzepatide lost less lean mass than those on tirzepatide alone.

healthcare.why: Practical evidence for how to support patients on obesity drugs.

pharma.why: Lean-mass loss is a key concern for incretin therapies and muscle-sparing rivals.

b01a6623c56d.summary: Researchers built a gait foundation model from 3D motion data of 3,328 deeply phenotyped adults; its embeddings significantly predicted 1,887 of 3,210 health phenotypes (Nature Medicine).

ai.why: Foundation model turning movement data into health predictions.

meddevices.why: Depth-camera gait analysis could become a screening tool.

diagnostics.why: Points to gait as a multisystem biomarker.

extra.title: Japan's Astellas Pharma inks $400M deal with AI Proteins to develop miniprotein therapeutics
extra.summary: Astellas signed a research collaboration and licence agreement with US computational protein design company AI Proteins, which is eligible for more than $400 million in upfront and milestone payments plus royalties. AI Proteins will design miniproteins against several targets and Astellas takes an exclusive worldwide licence to the candidates.

ai.why: De novo computational protein design backed by a large pharma deal.

pharma.why: Japanese pharma buys into a new therapeutic modality.

investment.why: $400M+ in potential payments for a private AI biotech.

extra.title: Singapore launches national reference to guide clinical investigations of medical devices
extra.summary: Singapore published Technical Reference TR 151:2026 on clinical investigation of medical devices, setting out what a device study application should contain and how to apply ISO 14155:2026 locally. It is meant to make ethics review more predictable, since most existing trial guidance was written for medicines.

meddevices.why: Clear national rules for running device trials in Singapore.

healthcare.why: Faster, more predictable device studies.

diagnostics.why: Applies to diagnostic devices studied clinically.

extra.title: Singapore's biopharma manufacturers launch S$4.8M study award for manufacturing careers
extra.summary: The Biopharmaceutical Manufacturers' Advisory Council launched a S$4.8 million study award expected to reach about 1,000 polytechnic and ITE students over five years, with cash awards of S$3,000-5,000 and priority internships at member companies.

bioprocessing.why: Workforce pipeline for biopharma manufacturing in a major hub.

pharma.why: Industry investment in local skills.

extra.title: Samsung Bioepis targets 20 biosimilars by 2030, eyes ADC and obesity drugs
extra.summary: Samsung Bioepis plans to grow from 11 marketed biosimilars to 20 by 2030 and is eyeing ADCs and obesity drugs; it filed in Korea in August for SB27, a Keytruda biosimilar.

pharma.why: Biosimilar pipeline targets originals with about 114 trillion won in 2025 sales, including Keytruda.

bioprocessing.why: Expansion by one of the largest biologics manufacturing groups.

extra.title: ECDC update: Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) outbreak, multi-country, 2026
extra.summary: ECDC updated its tracker of the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak on 26 October: DRC had reported 9,552 confirmed cases and 4,602 related deaths across eight provinces by 18 October, and Nigeria reported a case on 20 October in a traveller from Uganda, with 53 contacts identified.

biosecurity.why: Large Ebola outbreak now with exported cases in Nigeria and Kenya.

healthcare.why: Major public health emergency in Africa with imported-case risk elsewhere.

pharma.why: No licensed vaccine for Bundibugyo virus; trials are under way.

diagnostics.why: Need for testing at borders and in affected countries.

extra.title: Kaigene signs agreement worth up to $580M with Korea's Celltrion for anti-APRIL antibody KG013
extra.summary: Celltrion took exclusive worldwide rights to Kaigene's half-life-extended anti-APRIL antibody KG013, initially for IgA nephropathy; Kaigene is eligible for up to $580.5 million including an undisclosed upfront and milestones, plus royalties.

pharma.why: Korean biologics giant buys into a novel antibody for a hot kidney disease target.

investment.why: Up to $580M deal for a US biotech.

extra.title: Waters and Labcorp to expand access to cervical cancer screening
extra.summary: Labcorp and Waters will offer the FDA-approved BD Onclarity HPV assay, which separately identifies six high-risk HPV types, through Labcorp's US network from late 2026, including its consumer channel.

diagnostics.why: Extended HPV genotyping rolled out by a national lab.

healthcare.why: Aims to close the US cervical screening gap.

extra.title: Enhertu approved in the EU as adjuvant treatment for patients with residual disease after neoadjuvant treatment for HER2-positive early breast cancer
extra.summary: The European Commission approved AstraZeneca and Daiichi Sankyo's Enhertu for HER2-positive early breast cancer with residual disease after neoadjuvant treatment. AstraZeneca says in the DESTINY-Breast05 phase 3 trial it cut the risk of invasive recurrence or death by 53% versus T-DM1 (3-year IDFS 92.4% vs 83.7%).

pharma.why: Moves a leading ADC into the curative early-disease setting in Europe.

healthcare.why: Changes standard care for high-risk early breast cancer patients.

extra.title: Korea's biohealth exports hit record $24.8 billion as cosmetics surge 31%
extra.summary: South Korea's biohealth exports rose 19.4% to a record $24.75B in the first nine months of 2026, per KHIDI; pharmaceuticals grew 14.2% to $8.93B, led by biopharmaceuticals at $5.71B, while pharma exports to the US fell 30%.

pharma.why: Korean biologics and biosimilar exports keep growing.

bioprocessing.why: Reflects Korea's CDMO and biosimilar manufacturing scale.

meddevices.why: Device exports up 6.2% to $4.7B.

extra.title: Asundexian first Factor XIa inhibitor approved in China for stroke risk reduction after priority review
extra.summary: China approved Bayer's once-daily asundexian (Sunharbo) to reduce stroke risk after non-cardioembolic ischaemic stroke or high-risk TIA, the first approval for a Factor XIa inhibitor; Bayer says it cut ischaemic stroke by 26% without more bleeding in the 12,327-patient OCEANIC-STROKE trial.

pharma.why: First-ever approval for the Factor XIa class of blood thinners.

healthcare.why: New secondary stroke prevention option without added bleeding.

investment.why: Key growth asset for Bayer; other filings under review.

extra.title: Korea to Nurture 200 Pharma and Biotech Ventures by 2030
extra.summary: South Korea's health and SME ministries launched the K-Pharma-Bio Frontier Company programme, selecting 50 ventures a year to reach 200 by 2030, with 60 billion won of investment and 90 billion won of guarantees over three years.

investment.why: State capital and guarantees for Korean biotech startups.

pharma.why: 40% of slots go to new drug developers.

meddevices.why: 20 slots for digital health and device firms.

bioprocessing.why: 10 slots for biomaterials and production technology.

extra.title: Australia's Audax Biosciences inks immuno-oncology deal worth $1.34 B with Astellas Pharma
extra.summary: Astellas took an exclusive option and licence on DAX-044, Australian biotech Audax Biosciences' IL-12 antibody-cytokine fusion, paying $285 million in upfront and option payments with up to $1.05 billion in milestones plus royalties; Audax will run a phase 1 study expected to start in 2027.

pharma.why: Large option deal for an engineered cytokine in oncology.

investment.why: Australian biotech lands a $1.34 billion-value agreement with a Japanese major.

extra.title: PDRadiopharma injects JPY 16.5 B into new manufacturing facility in Japan
extra.summary: PeptiDream's subsidiary PDRadiopharma will spend about 16.5 billion yen on a radiopharmaceutical plant at Kazusa Akademia Park in Chiba, with construction starting in 2027 and completion in 2028, for domestic supply and Asia-Pacific exports.

bioprocessing.why: New radiopharmaceutical manufacturing capacity in Japan.

pharma.why: Supply base for a fast-growing radioligand therapy market.

investment.why: Large capital commitment funded by bank loans and incentives.

extra.title: Singapore approves Merck's CAPVAXIVE 21-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine
extra.summary: Singapore's Health Sciences Authority has approved Merck's 21-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine CAPVAXIVE for adults aged 18 and over, covering serotypes responsible for most invasive pneumococcal disease in adults.

pharma.why: Asian market access for a next-generation adult pneumococcal vaccine.

healthcare.why: Wider adult pneumococcal protection in Singapore.

extra.title: GC Biopharma gets MFDS approval for Hunterase ICV
extra.summary: Korea's MFDS approved GC Biopharma's Hunterase ICV, an enzyme therapy injected into the brain's ventricles for Hunter syndrome patients with central nervous system symptoms; the company says it is the first treatment approved in Korea for those symptoms, used alongside the intravenous form.

pharma.why: Intracerebroventricular delivery solves the blood-brain barrier problem for an enzyme therapy.

healthcare.why: First Korean option for neurological Hunter syndrome.

extra.title: Indian regulators order Sun Pharma to halt eye-drug production at Assam plant over quality lapses
extra.summary: India's CDSCO and the Assam drugs controller ordered Sun Pharma to stop making, selling and distributing ophthalmic products from its Kokjhar plant in Assam after a joint inspection found quality management system failures, naming products including Lotepred, Nepalact OD, Nepalact-Z, Brinzotim and Depopred. Production cannot resume until a satisfactory compliance report is accepted; the company has filed one and regulators are reviewing it.

pharma.why: Manufacturing halt at India's largest drugmaker over GMP failures.

healthcare.why: Supply of several prescription eye medicines is suspended.

bioprocessing.why: Sterile ophthalmic manufacturing quality systems under scrutiny.

extra.title: DKSH to acquire NewBridge Pharmaceuticals for $390 million to build a MENA healthcare platform
extra.summary: DKSH agreed to buy 100% of Dubai-based NewBridge Pharmaceuticals at an enterprise value of $390 million, extending its healthcare outsourcing business beyond Asia Pacific into 14 Middle East and North Africa markets. NewBridge, which provides market access, medical affairs and sales services for specialty and rare disease medicines, is expected to post net sales of about $385 million in 2027 at a high single-digit EBITDA margin.

pharma.why: Commercialisation route for specialty and rare disease drugs in MENA.

investment.why: $390m enterprise value acquisition expanding a distribution platform.

healthcare.why: Market access infrastructure for innovative medicines in the region.

extra.title: Waters builds AI peak integration into Empower chromatography software
extra.summary: Waters added AI-powered peak integration to Empower, its chromatography data system for regulated laboratories, saying it cuts manual effort and variability in late-stage development and QC while keeping data inside the validated environment. Early access enrolment starts in December 2026 and validated deployment is expected in mid-2027; Waters says the strategy targets around 500,000 Empower users.

ai.why: AI embedded in a regulated GxP data system rather than a research tool.

bioprocessing.why: Analytical QC workflows in pharmaceutical manufacturing.

pharma.why: Late-stage development and release testing.

extra.title: ECDC update: Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) outbreak passes 10,000 confirmed cases in DRC
extra.summary: ECDC's 30 October update reports 10,274 confirmed cases and 4,992 related deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo as of 29 October, up from 9,552 cases and 4,602 deaths in its 26 October update, with community transmission ongoing. Imported cases have been reported in Kenya and Nigeria.

biosecurity.why: The Bundibugyo outbreak is still growing by hundreds of confirmed cases a week, with exported cases in two other African countries.

healthcare.why: A large public health emergency with medical evacuations to Europe.

pharma.why: There is still no licensed Bundibugyo vaccine or treatment, and trials are under way.

diagnostics.why: Sustained need for confirmatory testing in DRC and for screening travellers.

extra.title: TRANSFORM II: sirolimus-coated balloon noninferior to drug-eluting stent at 1 year
extra.summary: In TRANSFORM II, presented at TCT 2026, 1,842 patients with coronary disease were randomised to Concept Medical's MagicTouch sirolimus-coated balloon or an everolimus-eluting stent; 12-month target lesion failure was 2.1% versus 2.4%, meeting noninferiority. It is one of the largest randomised tests of a leave-nothing-behind approach in native coronary vessels.

meddevices.why: Large randomised evidence that a drug-coated balloon can match a stent, a potential shift in the coronary device market.

healthcare.why: Could let more patients be treated without a permanent metal implant.

extra.title: P4 trial: CT angiography noninferior to IVUS for guiding PCI
extra.summary: The P4 trial randomised 1,105 patients to PCI planned with coronary CT angiography or guided by intravascular ultrasound; 12-month target-vessel failure was 4.1% versus 4.6%, meeting noninferiority. Results were presented at TCT 2026 and published in the New England Journal of Medicine.

meddevices.why: Supports CT-based planning as an alternative to intravascular imaging catheters in PCI.

healthcare.why: Could change how cardiology teams plan stenting procedures.

diagnostics.why: Expands the role of cardiac CT imaging from diagnosis into procedure planning.

extra.title: Coronary sinus Reducer shows no perfusion benefit in sham-controlled ANOCA trial
extra.summary: In the single-centre REMEDY-PILOT study of 54 patients with angina and non-obstructed coronary arteries, J&J MedTech's Shockwave Reducer did not change myocardial perfusion reserve at 6 months versus a sham procedure (P = 0.72). The results were presented at TCT 2026.

meddevices.why: A sham-controlled setback for expanding the Reducer into microvascular angina.

healthcare.why: Bears on treatment options for angina without obstructive coronary disease.

extra.title: Women travel thousands of miles for a reproductive moonshot. Scientists say they've been misled
extra.summary: A STAT investigation found US facilitator International Fertility Group sent older women, mostly to a clinic in Albania, for mitochondrial replacement therapy marketed as boosting 'egg energy', claiming 34 births and a 54% pregnancy rate it did not substantiate. Experts say there is no published evidence the technique works for women over 40; after STAT's inquiries IFG paused new enrolment.

healthcare.why: Exposes unproven embryo-modification procedures sold to infertility patients through medical tourism.

cellgene.why: Germline mitochondrial transfer is being used outside regulated settings, raising oversight questions for the field.

extra.title: Neurocrine defends Prader-Willi drug after another patient death
extra.summary: Neurocrine confirmed another death in a patient taking its Prader-Willi syndrome drug Vykat XR, which BioSpace says would bring reported deaths to eight; clinicians say the events are not definitively linked to the drug. Neurocrine says it is confident in the benefit-risk profile and current label, and plans a dosing and safety study in 2027.

pharma.why: Post-marketing safety pressure on a drug Neurocrine bought with its $2.9 billion Soleno acquisition.

healthcare.why: Prescribers of a rare-disease drug face mounting safety signals.

investment.why: Vykat brought in $107 million in Q3 and analysts expect discontinuations.

extra.title: Pfizer eyes Europe first for Lyme vaccine as prevalence rises in US
extra.summary: Pfizer expects Europe to be the first market for its Valneva-partnered Lyme disease vaccine PF-07307405: the EMA accepted the application in August with a CHMP opinion due in 2027, while a US filing has not yet been made and an update on FDA talks is expected this quarter.

pharma.why: Path to market for the only late-stage Lyme vaccine.

healthcare.why: First Lyme vaccine for people in decades could reach Europe before the US.

extra.title: Amgen starts MariTide autoinjector study as pivotal readouts approach
extra.summary: Amgen has started a phase 3 trial of home self-injection of its obesity drug MariTide with an autoinjector, part of the 10-trial MARITIME programme; the first phase 3 results are expected in 2027 and analysts say tolerability is the key question.

pharma.why: Late-stage progress for a leading next-generation obesity drug.

meddevices.why: Autoinjector delivery for a less frequently dosed drug.

extra.title: Merck, Moderna serve 99% of trial patients with mRNA vaccine as personalized shots near market
extra.summary: In the phase 3 INTerpath-001 melanoma trial (1,137 patients, hazard ratio 0.58 for recurrence or death), 99% of patients in the vaccine arm received a manufactured personalised intismeran vaccine, Merck and Moderna said, showing the bespoke shots can be made at global scale.

cellgene.why: Shows individualised mRNA cancer vaccines can be manufactured reliably across many countries.

pharma.why: Clears a practical hurdle before a likely launch with Keytruda.

bioprocessing.why: Per-patient manufacturing worked for 99% of patients.

extra.title: FDA grants accelerated approval to amivantamab and hyaluronidase for previously treated HNSCC
extra.summary: The FDA on 5 November gave accelerated approval to J&J's subcutaneous Rybrevant Faspro (amivantamab) as a single agent for recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma that progressed after platinum chemotherapy and a PD-(L)1 antibody, excluding HPV-associated oropharyngeal cancer. In the 102-patient OrigAMI-4 cohort the response rate was 42%, and 56% of responses lasted at least six months.

pharma.why: First approval for the EGFR-MET bispecific outside lung cancer, in a setting where current options give about 20% response.

healthcare.why: A new option for patients with relapsed head and neck cancer.
